01Security (Part 2)

What is DevSecOps?

Pehle security aakhri me aati thi — release se ek din pehle ek team aake kehti 'ye insecure hai, wapas jao'. DevSecOps ka matlab hai security ko shuruaat se, har step me, har developer ki zimmedari bana dena — Dev + Sec + Ops, ek hi flow me.

1. DevSecOps kya hai? — ghar banane wali kahani

Ghar bante waqt agar darwaze aur taale aakhri me lagaye jaayein to kya hoga? Deewarein todni padengi, kharcha double, aur tab tak chor aaram se ghus chuke honge. Samajhdar builder neev dalte waqt hi security sochta hai — majboot darwaze, sahi wiring, safe jagah.

DevSecOps wahi soch hai software ke liye: security ko end me audit nahi, shuru se design banao. Developer code likhte waqt hi secure likhe, pipeline khud vulnerabilities pakde, aur production me har cheez monitor hoti rahe. Security kisi ek team ka kaam nahi — shared responsibility hai.

Shift-left: Security ko lifecycle me 'left' — matlab shuruaat ki taraf — shift karo. Bug jitna pehle milega, fix utna sasta hoga. Production me mila bug, development me mile bug se 30x mehenga padta hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

DevOps se DevSecOps tak

DevOps ne dev aur ops ke beech ki deewar tod di — ab code jaldi release hota hai. Par security peeche reh gayi: fast release = fast vulnerabilities bhi. DevSecOps usi gap ko bharta hai.

Farq simple hai: DevOps me security ek alag gate tha (release se pehle), DevSecOps me security har gate ka hissa hai — code likhte waqt, commit karte waqt, build karte waqt, deploy karte waqt.

Sahi: Security checks pipeline me automated — har PR pe SAST scan, har build pe dependency scan.
Galat: 'Security team dekh legi' bolke insecure code merge karna — wahi purana silo, naya naam.

Pipeline me security kahan?

Har stage pe ek security check banta hai: Code — IDE plugin (SAST) insecure pattern likhte hi warn kare. Commit — pre-commit hook secrets (API keys) ko rok de. Build — dependency scan (SCA) jaane-mane vulnerable library pakde. Test — DAST running app ko attack karke dekhe. Deploy — infrastructure as code scan (misconfigured S3 bucket pakdo). Run — runtime monitoring aur alerting.

Ye saare checks automated hone chahiye — manual review har PR pe possible nahi.

SAST, DAST, SCA — teeno alag kyun?

SAST (Static): Source code ko bina chalaye scan karta hai — SQL injection pattern, hardcoded password. Jaldi milta hai, par false positive zyada.

DAST (Dynamic): Chalti hui app ko test karta hai — jaise hacker karega. Real vulnerabilities pakadta hai, par late milta hai.

SCA (Software Composition): Third-party libraries check karta hai — tumhare code me 80% code to libraries ka hai! Log4Shell jaisi vulnerability SCA hi pakadta hai.

Teeno chahiye: SAST code ki galti, SCA library ki galti, DAST runtime ki galti pakadta hai. Ek se kaam nahi chalega.

Culture — sabse mushkil hissa

Tools kharidna aasan hai, culture badalna mushkil. DevSecOps me developer ko ye samajhna padta hai ki security uski bhi zimmedari hai, aur security team ko developer ki speed samajhni padti hai.

Kaam karne wale tareeke: security champions (har team me ek trained developer), blameless postmortem (galti pe daant nahi, fix pe focus), aur security ko enabler banao — 'ye mat karo' ki jagah 'ye secure tareeka hai' batao.

Sahi: Security team pipeline me guardrails banati hai, roadblock nahi.

3. DevSecOps toolkit — stage ke hisaab se

StageCheckTools (examples)
Code likhte waqtSAST, secret detectionSonarQube, Semgrep, gitleaks, IDE plugins
DependenciesSCA — known CVEsDependabot, Snyk, Trivy
Build / ImageContainer scanTrivy, Grype, Docker Scout
Infra as CodeMisconfigurationCheckov, tfsec, Terrascan
RuntimeDAST, monitoringOWASP ZAP, Falco, SIEM

Har tool ka result pipeline me gate bane: critical vulnerability = build fail. Par pehle 'warn-only' mode se shuru karo — ek din me sab fail kar doge to team tools ko bypass karne lagegi.

# Trivy se Docker image scan — CI me ek line
trivy image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL myapp:latest
# CRITICAL mila to exit code 1 → pipeline fail

4. Try karo — ek vulnerable build pakdo

Ek PR aaya hai jisme ek purani library aur ek hardcoded API key hai. Pipeline ke security gates chalao aur dekho kya pakda jata hai.

  1. 1. Secret scan (pre-commit)
  2. 2. SAST scan (code)
  3. 3. SCA scan (dependencies)
  4. 4. Sab fix karke dobara chalao

5. DevOps vs DevSecOps — ek table me

CheezDevOpsDevSecOps
Security kab?Release se pehle, alag teamHar stage pe, automated
ZimmedariSecurity team kiSabki — shared responsibility
SpeedFast releaseFast + safe release
Bug costLate milta hai, mehenga fixEarly milta hai, sasta fix
ToolsCI/CD, monitoringCI/CD + SAST/DAST/SCA + IaC scan

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Security ko sirf tool samajhna: Snyk kharid liya, culture nahi badla — to alerts ignore honge. Tool + training + process, teeno chahiye.
  2. Ek din me sab gates 'fail' par laga dena: 500 purani vulnerabilities ek saath aayengi, team bypass karne lagegi. Pehle warn-only, phir dheere-dheere strict.
  3. Secrets ko repo me chhodna: Git history se secret kabhi nahi marta — key leak hote hi rotate karo, sirf delete karna kaafi nahi.
  4. Sirf apna code scan karna: 80% code third-party libraries ka hai — SCA ke bina tum andhere me ho.
  5. Compliance ko security samajhna: Checklist tick karna ≠ secure hona. Audit pass karna aur real attack rokna alag cheezein hain.

7. Interview corner

Q: DevSecOps aur DevOps me kya farq hai?

DevOps dev + ops ko jodta hai speed ke liye; DevSecOps usme security ko shuru se jodta hai — automated SAST/DAST/SCA checks, secret scanning, aur shared responsibility. Security end ka gate nahi, har stage ka hissa hai.

Q: Shift-left security ka matlab kya hai?

Security ko lifecycle me pehle le aana — design aur coding stage pe hi vulnerabilities pakadna. Jitna pehle bug milega, utna sasta fix hoga; production me mila bug sabse mehenga padta hai.

Q: SAST, DAST aur SCA me farq batao.

SAST source code ko bina chalaye scan karta hai; DAST chalti hui app ko attack karke test karta hai; SCA third-party libraries/dependencies me known vulnerabilities dhoondhta hai. Teeno alag tarah ki galtiyan pakadte hain.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: DevSecOps me 'shift-left' ka matlab kya hai?

  • Security ko release ke baad karna
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Security ko lifecycle ki shuruaat me le aana
  • Security team ko hata dena
  • Sirf firewall lagana

Sawaal 2: Log4Shell jaisi library vulnerability kaunsa scan pakadta hai?

  • SAST
  • DAST
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: SCA (dependency scan)
  • Unit test
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: DevSecOps = security ko shuru se, har stage pe, automated tareeke se pipeline me daal dena; SAST code, SCA libraries, DAST runtime ko check karta hai; culture badle bina tools kaam nahi karte.

DevSecOps ke 10 key concepts (original guide se)

DevSecOps DevOps ka natural evolution hai — Development (Dev) + Security (Sec) + Operations (Ops) ka convergence. Matlab security ko software development aur deployment ke poore lifecycle me daal do. Guide ke 10 key concepts ye hain:

  • Automated Security Checks: Security checks ko pipeline me automate karo — har commit aur har build pe apne aap chalein.
  • Continuous Monitoring: System ko hamesha monitor karo — naya threat ya anomaly dikhte hi alert aaye.
  • CI/CD Automation: Build, test aur deploy automate karo, taaki security checks bhi har release ke saath chalein.
  • Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Infrastructure ko code ki tarah likho aur version karo — misconfiguration review ho sake.
  • Container Security: Container images ko scan karo — kamzor base image ya vulnerable library production me na jaye.
  • Secret Management: Passwords, API keys aur certificates ko secret manager me rakho — code ya repo me kabhi nahi.
  • Threat Modeling: Design karte time hi socho — attacker kahan se ghus sakta hai, aur kya-kya nuksaan ho sakta hai.
  • Quality Assurance (QA) Integration: QA ke saath security testing bhi jodo — functional test ke saath security test bhi chale.
  • Collaboration and Communication: Dev, Sec aur Ops teeno ek saath kaam karein — security kisi ek team ki zimmedari nahi, sabki hai.
  • Vulnerability Management: Kamzoriyan dhoondho, priority lagao, aur time pe fix karo — scan karke chhodna kaafi nahi.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/what-is-devsecops.md

02Security (Part 2)

Is PassKey Shaping a Passwordless Future?

Password yaad rakhna, reset karna, leak hona — ye sab khatam ho sakta hai? Passkeys (FIDO2/WebAuthn) ka vaada yahi hai: password hi nahi hoga. Tumhare phone ya laptop me ek private key rehti hai, site pe sirf public key — login karne ke liye bas fingerprint ya face se confirm karo.

1. Passkey kya hai? — taala-chabhi wali kahani

Socho har website ke liye tumhare paas ek alag taala-chabhi ka joda hai. Taala (public key) tum website ko de dete ho, chabhi (private key) tumhare phone me rehti hai — kabhi bahar nahi nikalti. Login karte waqt website kehti hai 'taala kholo', tumhara phone chabhi se khol ke dikhata hai — par chabhi kisi ko deta nahi.

Password system me tum chabhi (password) har baar website ko bhej dete the — aur website use apne paas rakh leti thi. Website hack hui to chabhi chori. Passkey me chabhi kabhi phone se bahar nahi jati — isliye server hack hone se bhi kuch nahi bigadta, aur phishing bhi nahi hoti: fake site ko tum chabhi de hi nahi sakte.

Core idea: Password = secret jo share karna padta hai. Passkey = private key jo kabhi share nahi hoti; sirf uska proof share hota hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Kaise kaam karta hai? — public key crypto

Passkey asymmetric cryptography pe based hai. Registration ke waqt tumhara device ek key pair banata hai: private key (device ke secure enclave/TPM me, kabhi bahar nahi nikalti) aur public key (server pe store hoti hai).

Login ke waqt: server ek random challenge bhejta hai → device use private key se sign karta hai (pehle tum fingerprint/face/PIN se confirm karte ho) → server public key se signature verify karta hai. Challenge har baar naya hota hai, to replay attack nahi hota.

Phishing-proof kyun? Challenge me site ka domain (origin) bhi sign hota hai. Fake site githb.com ka challenge tumhara device sign hi nahi karega — kyunki passkey github.com ke liye bani thi.

Password se behtar kyun?

1) Phishing-proof: Password type karke fake site ko de sakte ho; passkey galat domain pe kaam hi nahi karti. 2) Leak-proof: Server pe sirf public key hai — leak hone se kuch nahi milta. 3) Yaad rakhna nahi: Koi password nahi, koi reset nahi. 4) Fast: Face ID se 2 second me login.

Google, Apple, Microsoft — sab passkeys support karte hain. Google ke data ke mutabik passkey login password se 2x fast aur 4x kam fail hota hai.

Sahi: Passkey + device ka screen lock (biometric/PIN) — dono mil ke strong authentication banate hain.

Sync vs device-bound — farq samjho

Device-bound passkey: Private key sirf ek device pe rehti hai (security key / YubiKey jaisi). Sabse secure, par device kho gaya to passkey bhi gayi — recovery ka alag plan chahiye.

Synced passkey: Private key tumhare cloud account (iCloud Keychain / Google Password Manager) se devices ke beech end-to-end encrypted sync hoti hai. Phone badlo to bhi passkey mil jati hai. Convenience zyada, par trust cloud provider pe bhi hai.

Aaj zyadatar log synced passkeys use karte hain — kyunki recovery aasan hai. High-security kaam (admin accounts) ke liye device-bound + hardware key behtar hai.

Challenges — passwordless future door kyun hai?

1) Recovery: Phone kho gaya aur cloud backup nahi to account lock ho sakta hai — har site ka recovery flow alag hai. 2) Sab sites support nahi karti: Aaj bhi zyadatar sites password mangti hain; transition saalon ka hai. 3) Shared devices: Cyber cafe ya family computer pe passkey use karna mushkil. 4) Samajh: Aam user ko 'key pair' samajhna mushkil — UX ko aur simple hona hai.

Isliye future hybrid hoga: passkey primary, password + 2FA backup ke roop me — dheere-dheere password peeche hatega, ek din me nahi.

Interview line: Passkeys passwords ko replace nahi kar rahe — wo password ki zaroorat ko khatam kar rahe hain, public-key crypto + biometrics se.

3. Registration aur login — step by step

REGISTRATION (pehli baar):
1. User: "Passkey banao" dabata hai
2. Server: random challenge + user id bhejta hai
3. Device: biometric/PIN se user confirm karta hai
4. Device: naya key pair banata hai (private key secure enclave me)
5. Device: public key + signed challenge server ko bhejta hai
6. Server: public key ko user account se jod ke store karta hai
LOGIN (har baar):
1. Server: naya random challenge bhejta hai
2. Device: Face ID / fingerprint se confirm
3. Device: challenge ko private key se sign karta hai
4. Server: public key se signature verify karta hai → login ✓

Note: Biometric data (fingerprint/face) kabhi server ko nahi jata — wo sirf device ko unlock karta hai. Server ko sirf signature milta hai.

4. Try karo — passkey login vs password login

Dono tareekon se login karke dekho — aur ek phishing attack bhi try karo. Kaunsa tareeka bachta hai?

  1. 1. Password se login karo
  2. 2. Passkey se login karo
  3. 3. Phishing attack — password
  4. 4. Phishing attack — passkey
  5. 5. Phone kho gaya — recovery

5. Password vs Passkey vs Password+2FA

CheezPasswordPassword + 2FAPasskey
Phishing-proof?❌ Nahi⚠ Partial (SMS OTP phish ho sakta hai)✅ Haan
Server leak se khatra?✅ Haan (hash crack)⚠ Kam❌ Public key bekaar hai
Yaad rakhna?Padta haiPadta hai + codeNahi
SpeedSlowSlowFast (2 sec)
RecoveryEmail resetBackup codesCloud sync / backup key

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Passkey ko 'ek aur password' samajhna: Ye password nahi hai — private key hai jo kabhi share nahi hoti. Iska mental model alag hai.
  2. Recovery plan na banana: Phone kho gaya aur backup nahi — account lock. Passkey banate hi recovery option set karo.
  3. Biometric = passkey samajhna: Fingerprint sirf device unlock karta hai; asli authentication key pair karta hai. Biometric server ko kabhi nahi jata.
  4. Har site pe passkey force karna: Abhi sab sites support nahi karti — password fallback rakhna practical hai, use hatao mat.
  5. Shared device pe passkey banana: Kisi aur ke computer pe passkey bana li to private key usi device pe reh jayegi. Sirf apne devices pe banao.

7. Interview corner

Q: Passkey password se behtar kyun hai?

Teen wajah: (1) Phishing-proof — passkey galat domain pe kaam nahi karti. (2) Leak-proof — server pe sirf public key hoti hai, jo bekaar hai. (3) Kuch yaad nahi rakhna — login biometric se 2 second me hota hai.

Q: Passkey me private key kahan rehti hai?

Device ke secure enclave/TPM me — hardware-isolated, kabhi bahar nahi nikalti. Login ke waqt device challenge ko andar hi sign karta hai; server ko sirf signature milta hai.

Q: Agar phone kho jaye to passkey ka kya hoga?

Synced passkey (iCloud/Google) ho to naye device pe cloud login se wapas mil jati hai. Device-bound ho to recovery code ya backup authenticator chahiye — isliye recovery plan pehle se set karna zaroori hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Passkey login me server ko kya milta hai?

  • Tumhara password
  • Tumhari fingerprint
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Private key se sign kiya hua challenge
  • Tumhara phone number

Sawaal 2: Passkey phishing-proof kyun hai?

  • Password lamba hota hai
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Passkey sirf sahi domain (origin) ke liye kaam karti hai
  • Site ko password dikhta nahi
  • Fingerprint use hota hai
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Passkey = device me private key + server pe public key; login = challenge sign karo, password kabhi travel nahi karta; phishing-proof aur leak-proof; recovery plan zaroor banao.

PassKey kaise kaam karta hai — How PassKeys Work (original guide se)

Google ne Android aur Chrome ke liye PassKey support announce kiya hai. Passkey ko Apple aur Microsoft bhi support karte hain, aur ise password ka safer replacement mana jata hai.

  • Step 1 — Create PassKeys: User account information confirm karta hai aur apne credentials present karta hai (face ID, touch ID, etc.). Website ke public key ke basis pe ek private key generate hoti hai. Private key device pe store hoti hai.
  • Step 2 — Sign in with PassKeys: User website pe sign in karte time generated private key use karta hai — bas account select karo aur credentials present karke private key unlock karo.

Iska natija: password leak ka risk hi nahi hai, kyunki websites ke databases me password store hi nahi hota. Passkeys industry standards pe bane hain aur alag-alag platforms aur browsers pe kaam karte hain — Windows, macOS, iOS aur ChromeOS — uniform user experience ke saath.

Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/is-passkey-shaping-a-passwordless-future.md

03Security (Part 2)

Cookies vs Sessions

Login karne ke baad website tumhe har page pe kaise pehchanti hai? Iske peeche do dost kaam karte hain — Cookie (browser me chhota sa note) aur Session (server pe tumhara record). Dono ka kaam ek hai — tumhe yaad rakhna — par tareeka bilkul alag.

1. Cookie vs Session — coat-check wali kahani

Cookie: Socho ek club tumhe entry pe ek stamp laga deta hai. Stamp tumhare haath pe hai — tum use leke ghumte ho, aur har baar gate pe dikha dete ho. Club ko tumhara naam yaad rakhne ki zaroorat nahi — stamp hi kaafi hai. Par stamp koi aur bhi dekh sakta hai ya copy kar sakta hai.

Session: Socho ek coat-check counter hai. Tum apna coat dete ho, wo tumhe ek token number deta hai (jaise #42). Tumhara coat (data) counter ke peeche safe rakha hai, tumhare paas sirf number hai. Number chori ho jaye to bhi coat tabhi milega jab counter wala number match kare — aur wo number har baar badla bhi ja sakta hai.

Ek line me: Cookie = data browser me rehta hai. Session = data server pe rehta hai, browser me sirf session ID (token number) rehta hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Cookie kya hai?

Cookie ek chhota sa text file hai jo server browser ko deta hai, aur browser use store karke har request ke saath wapas bhejta hai. Server Set-Cookie: theme=dark bhejta hai, browser har request me Cookie: theme=dark bhejta hai.

Cookies ka use: preferences (theme, language), tracking, aur kabhi-kabhi login token rakhne ke liye. Size limit ~4KB hoti hai, aur har request ke saath jaati hain — isliye inme zyada data mat rakho.

Security flags: HttpOnly (JavaScript cookie ko padh nahi sakta — XSS se bachao), Secure (sirf HTTPS pe bhejega), SameSite (doosri site se request pe cookie nahi bhejega — CSRF se bachao).

Session kya hai?

Session server pe store hota hai: user login karta hai → server ek session ID banata hai (random, lamba) → use DB/memory (Redis) me user ke data ke saath store karta hai → session ID browser ko cookie me de deta hai.

Har request pe browser sirf session ID bhejta hai, server us ID se apna record nikaalta hai: 'Ah, ye user #42 hai, iska cart ye hai, ye admin hai.' Data server pe hai, to user use dekh ya badal nahi sakta.

Session expire hota hai — 30 minute inactive rahe to khatam, ya logout pe delete. Server restart hua to memory wale sessions gayab — isliye production me Redis jaise external store use karte hain.

Dono kaise saath kaam karte hain?

Zyadatar apps dono ko saath use karte hain: session ID ko cookie me store karte hain! Cookie yahan sirf carrier hai (token number), asli data session store (server) me hai.

Flow: Login → server session banata hai → Set-Cookie: session_id=abc123; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax → browser har request me cookie bhejta hai → server session store se user nikaalta hai → response.

Is combo ke fayde: data server pe safe hai, browser pe sirf ek random ID hai, aur ID ko rotate/invalidate karna aasan hai (logout = session delete).

Kaunsa kab use karo?

Cookie (seedha data): Chhoti, non-sensitive preferences — theme, language, 'remember me' token (secure, signed). Session: Login state, cart, sensitive data — jo user ko dikhna nahi chahiye ya badalna nahi chahiye.

JWT: Session ka stateless alternative — data token me hi hota hai (signed). Microservices me popular hai, par revoke karna mushkil hai (ye agle pages me detail me hai).

Sahi: Sensitive data hamesha server side (session) rakho; cookie me sirf ID ya signed, non-sensitive data.
Galat: Cookie me isAdmin=true rakhna — user cookie edit karke admin ban jayega!

3. Side-by-side comparison

CheezCookieSession
Data kahan rehta hai?Browser (client) peServer pe (DB/Redis)
Size~4KB per cookieServer pe — badi ho sakti hai
SecurityUser dekh/badhal sakta haiUser data dekh nahi sakta
ExpiryBrowser band hone ya expiry date takTimeout ya logout pe
Server loadKam (data client pe)Zyada (har request pe lookup)
Multiple servers?Aasan (data client pe hai)Shared store (Redis) chahiye
# Express.js me session (connect-redis ke saath)
app.use(session({
  store: new RedisStore({ client: redis }),
  secret: 'keyboard cat', resave: false, saveUninitialized: false,
  cookie: { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'lax', maxAge: 3600000 }
}));
// req.session.userId = 42;  → server pe store, browser me sirf ID

4. Try karo — login karo, phir cookie edit karo

Pehle normal login karo. Phir ek attacker bano: cookie ko edit karke dekho kya hota hai — session wala system bachta hai ya cookie wala?

  1. 1. Login karo (session system)
  2. 2. Cookie edit karke admin bano (try karo)
  3. 3. Cookie wala system (galat design)
  4. 4. Logout karo

5. Cookie ke types — ek table me

TypeKaamExample
Session cookieBrowser band hote hi deleteLogin session ID
Persistent cookieExpiry date tak rehti hai'Remember me' (30 din)
First-partyUsi site ki jo tum khole hoSite ki theme
Third-partyDoosri site ki (ads/analytics)Facebook Pixel — browsers ab block karte hain
Secure / HttpOnlySecurity flagsHTTPS only + JS se hidden

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Cookie me sensitive data rakhna: isAdmin=true ya password cookie me — user edit kar sakta hai. Sensitive data server pe rakho.
  2. HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite flags bhoolna: Bina HttpOnly ke XSS se cookie chori; bina Secure ke HTTP pe leak; bina SameSite ke CSRF attack.
  3. Session ID ko predictable banana: Session ID random aur lamba hona chahiye (128-bit) — user_id ko hi session ID banana matlab koi bhi kisi ka session guess kar le.
  4. Session ko kabhi expire na karna: 'Remember me' ke alawa session ka timeout hona chahiye — chori hua session hamesha ke liye valid nahi rehna chahiye.
  5. Logout pe session delete na karna: Sirf cookie clear karna kaafi nahi — server pe session bhi delete karo, warna purani ID kaam karti rahegi.

7. Interview corner

Q: Cookie aur session me farq kya hai?

Cookie browser pe store hoti hai — data client pe rehta hai. Session server pe store hota hai — browser me sirf session ID rehti hai. Isliye sensitive data session me safe hai, cookie me nahi.

Q: Session ID ko cookie me kyun rakhte hain?

Kyunki HTTP stateless hai — har request nayi hoti hai. Cookie session ID ko har request ke saath server tak pahuncha deti hai, taaki server user ko pehchan sake. Cookie yahan sirf carrier hai.

Q: HttpOnly aur SameSite flags kyun zaroori hain?

HttpOnly JavaScript ko cookie padhne se rokta hai — XSS attack se session chori nahi hoti. SameSite doosri site se aane wali request pe cookie bhejne se rokta hai — CSRF attack rukta hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Session me user ka data kahan store hota hai?

  • Browser me
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Server pe (DB/Redis)
  • Cookie me plain text
  • URL me

Sawaal 2: Cookie me 'isAdmin=true' rakhna kyun galat hai?

  • Cookie bahut badi ho jati hai
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: User cookie edit karke admin ban sakta hai
  • Cookie slow hoti hai
  • Browser cookie delete kar deta hai
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Cookie = data browser me; Session = data server pe, browser me sirf ID; sensitive data hamesha server side; HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite flags zaroor lagao.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/what-are-the-differences-between-cookies-and-sessions.md
← PichhlaIs PassKey Shaping a Passwordless Future?Agla →Token, Cookie, Session
04Security (Part 2)

Token, Cookie, Session

Teen shabd, ek hi sawaal — 'website mujhe kaise pehchanti hai?' Token, Cookie aur Session teeno ka jawab alag tareeke se dete hain. Ye page in teeno ko ek saath, ek hi kahani me samjhata hai, taaki interview me kabhi confuse na ho.

1. Teeno ko ek hi kahani se samjho — concert wali kahani

Session: Concert me entry pe tumhara naam list me likha jata hai, aur tumhe ek number wala wristband milta hai. Andar ka saara record (tum kaun ho, VIP ho ya nahi) organizer ke register me hai — wristband sirf number hai.

Cookie: Wristband hi cookie hai — wo chhota sa token jo tumhare paas rehta hai aur har gate pe dikhana padta hai. Cookie ek carrier hai, data nahi.

Token (JWT): Is baar organizer tumhe ek card deta hai jisme sab kuch likha hai — naam, VIP status, expiry — aur neeche unka signature hai. Gate wala card padh ke, signature check karke andar jaane deta hai — register dekhne ki zaroorat hi nahi. Card kho jaye to koi bhi use kar sakta hai, jab tak expiry na ho.

Ek line me: Session = data server pe, ID client pe. Cookie = data le jaane ka tareeka. Token = data khud client pe, signed hua.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Session — server yaad rakhta hai

Login hote hi server ek session banata hai: user ka data (id, role, cart) server ke store (Redis/DB) me, aur browser ko sirf ek random session ID milta hai — aam taur pe cookie ke through.

Plus: Data server pe hai — user badal nahi sakta; logout = session delete, turant invalid; data kitna bhi bada ho sakta hai.

Minus: Har request pe server ko store lookup karna padta hai; multiple servers ho to shared store (Redis) chahiye; server restart pe memory sessions gayab.

Best for: Traditional web apps, jahan server pe control chahiye aur revoke karna aasan ho.

Token (JWT) — client khud saboot leke chalta hai

JWT ek self-contained token hai: teen hisse — Header, Payload (user id, role, expiry), Signature. Server secret key se sign karta hai, client use har request me Authorization: Bearer <token> header me bhejta hai.

Server ko koi lookup nahi karna — signature verify karo, payload padho, kaam ho gaya. Isliye JWT stateless hai aur microservices me popular hai: har service khud verify kar sakti hai.

Minus: Token revoke karna mushkil hai (expiry tak valid rehta hai); payload me sensitive data mat rakho (koi bhi decode kar sakta hai — sirf signature verify hoti hai, data chhupa nahi hota); token bada hota hai.

Cookie — carrier, data nahi

Cookie khud koi authentication mechanism nahi hai — ye ek storage + transport mechanism hai. Cookie me session ID bhi rakh sakte ho, JWT bhi rakh sakte ho.

Cookie ka fayda: browser automatically har request ke saath bhejta hai — JS code likhne ki zaroorat nahi. Isliye web apps me session ID cookie me rakhna standard hai.

Cookie ke nuksaan: CSRF attack (browser khud cookie bhej deta hai, attacker ki site se bhi) — isliye SameSite flag zaroori hai. Aur cookie size ~4KB hai.

Confusion door karo: 'Cookie vs Session' galat comparison hai — cookie session ID ko le jaane ka tareeka hai. Sahi comparison hai 'Session vs Token (JWT)'.

Teeno ka saath me flow

Session-based web app: Login → server session banata hai → session ID cookie me → har request: cookie → server lookup → allow.

Token-based API/mobile app: Login → server JWT deta hai → client use storage me rakhta hai → har request: Authorization header → server signature verify → allow.

Hybrid: JWT ko HttpOnly cookie me rakh do — browser automatic bhejega, JS padh nahi payega (XSS safe), par CSRF se bachne ke liye SameSite + CSRF token bhi chahiye.

Mobile apps me cookie nahi hoti (browser nahi hai) — wahan token (Authorization header) standard hai.

3. Kaunsa kab? — decision guide

ScenarioBest choiceKyun
Traditional server-rendered web appSession + CookieRevoke aasan, data server pe safe
Mobile app / SPA + APIJWT (Bearer token)Stateless, browser cookie nahi chahiye
MicroservicesJWTHar service khud verify kare, central lookup nahi
High security (banking)SessionTurant revoke, short expiry, server control
Third-party API accessOAuth tokenScoped, expiry, revoke possible
# JWT structure (teen hisse, dot se jude)
eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9  .  eyJ1c2VySWQiOjQyLCJyb2xlIjoidXNlciJ9  .  SflKxwRJSMeKKF2QT4fwpMeJf36POk6yJV_adQssw5c
   HEADER            .              PAYLOAD (base64 — padha ja sakta hai!)  .  SIGNATURE (secret se)

4. Try karo — teeno tareekon se login karo

Ek hi user, teen alag systems. Har ek me login karo, phir logout/revoke try karo — kaunsa turant rukta hai, kaunsa nahi?

  1. 1. Session login
  2. 2. JWT login
  3. 3. JWT logout (problem dekho)
  4. 4. Session logout (farq dekho)
  5. 5. Cookie me JWT rakhna (hybrid)

5. Teeno ka comparison table

CheezSessionToken (JWT)Cookie
Kya hai?Server-side recordSigned data, client peBrowser storage mechanism
Data kahan?Server peToken me (client pe)Browser me (chhota data)
Stateful?HaanNahi (stateless)—
RevokeTurantMushkil (expiry/blocklist)Delete karke
ScaleShared store chahiyeAasan (koi lookup nahi)—
Best forWeb apps, bankingAPIs, mobile, microservicesSession ID / token carrier

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. 'Cookie vs Session' ko alag-alag cheez samajhna: Cookie session ID ko le jaane ka tareeka hai — dono saath kaam karte hain, ek doosre ke alternative nahi.
  2. JWT payload me sensitive data rakhna: Payload sirf Base64 hai — koi bhi decode kar sakta hai. Password ya personal data kabhi payload me mat rakho.
  3. JWT ko bina expiry ke banana: Kabhi expire na hone wala token chori hone par hamesha kaam karega. Short expiry + refresh token use karo.
  4. Session ID ko guessable banana: Session ID random 128-bit honi chahiye — user_id ya timestamp ko session ID banana matlab session hijack.
  5. Logout pe sirf client-side token delete karna: Server-side session bhi delete karo — warna purani ID/token kaam karta rahega.

7. Interview corner

Q: Session aur JWT me main farq kya hai?

Session stateful hai — data server pe rehta hai, revoke turant hota hai, par har request pe lookup chahiye. JWT stateless hai — data token me rehta hai, server lookup nahi karta, par revoke karna mushkil hai. Web apps me session, APIs/microservices me JWT common hai.

Q: Cookie authentication hai ya nahi?

Cookie khud authentication nahi hai — ye ek storage/transport mechanism hai. Cookie me session ID ya JWT rakh sakte ho. Asli authentication server pe session lookup ya token signature verify se hoti hai.

Q: JWT ka payload secure hai?

Nahi — payload sirf Base64 encoded hota hai, encrypted nahi. Koi bhi decode karke padh sakta hai. Isliye payload me sirf non-sensitive data (user id, role, expiry) rakho; signature sirf ye guarantee karta hai ki data badla nahi gaya.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: JWT stateless kyun kaha jata hai?

  • Isme password nahi hota
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Server ko verify ke liye DB lookup nahi karna padta — signature hi kaafi hai
  • Ye cookie me nahi rehta
  • Ye expire nahi hota

Sawaal 2: Session-based system me logout turant kaam kyun karta hai?

  • Browser cookie delete ho jati hai
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Server apne store se session delete kar deta hai
  • Password badal jata hai
  • User ka naam bhool jata hai
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Session = data server pe, ID cookie me; Token (JWT) = signed data client pe, stateless; Cookie = carrier hai, authentication nahi; revoke chahiye to session, scale chahiye to JWT.

Identity management — simple se complex tak (original guide se)

Website pe login karte time teen cheezein hoti hain: pehle tum batate ho tum kaun ho (identification), phir tumhari pehchan verify hoti hai (authentication), aur phir tumhe zaroori permissions milti hain (authorization). Guide simple se complex tak 6 tareeke batata hai:

  1. WWW-Authenticate: Sabse basic tareeka — browser khud tumse username aur password maangta hai. Problem ye hai ki login life cycle ko control nahi kar sakte (logout ka button nahi hota), isliye aaj kal ye shayad hi use hota hai.
  2. Session-Cookie: Login life cycle pe behtar control — server session storage maintain karta hai aur browser ke paas sirf session ki ID hoti hai (cookie me). Problem: cookie aam taur pe sirf browsers ke saath kaam karti hai, mobile app ke saath friendly nahi hai.
  3. Token: Compatibility problem solve karta hai — client token server ko bhejta hai aur server use validate karta hai. Nuksaan ye hai ki token ko encrypt aur decrypt karna padta hai, jo time le sakta hai.
  4. JWT: Token ko represent karne ka standard tareeka — ye digitally signed hota hai, isliye is information ko verify aur trust kar sakte ho. Signature ki wajah se server ko session information save karne ki zaroorat nahi padti.
  5. SSO (Single Sign-On): Ek baar sign on karo aur multiple websites me login ho jao. Ye CAS (Central Authentication Service) use karta hai jo cross-site information maintain karta hai.
  6. OAuth 2.0: Isse tum ek website ko authorize kar sakte ho ki wo doosri website pe tumhari information access kare — jaise "Google se login karo" wala button.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/token-cookie-session.md

05Security (Part 2)

Top 6 Firewall Use Cases

Firewall sirf 'internet se bachao' ke liye nahi hai — uske 6 alag kaam hain, har ek ek alag problem solve karta hai. Is page me har use case ko real example ke saath samjho — taaki interview me 'firewall kahan use hota hai?' ka jawab ek line me na deke, ek kahani suna sako.

1. Firewall ke 6 kaam — ek sheher ki suraksha

Ek sheher ko sirf ek gate se suraksha nahi milti. Sheher me border check post (bahar se kaun aa raha hai), mohalla watch (andar kya ho raha hai), VIP zone (khaas jagah alag suraksha), traffic police (kaunsi gaadi kahan ja sakti hai), customs (andar kya le ja rahe ho) aur emergency block (khatra dikhte hi rasta band) — sab chahiye.

Firewall ke 6 use cases wahi 6 kaam hain: perimeter protection, internal segmentation, DMZ, access control, content filtering aur threat prevention. Har ek ka apna rule set aur apni jagah hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

1. Perimeter Protection — border security

Firewall ka sabse pehla kaam: bahari internet aur tumhare network ke beech deewar. Sirf zaroori traffic andar aaye — web server pe port 443, baaki sab block.

Example: Company ka office network — internet se sirf VPN aur web traffic aata hai, baaki har port band. Attacker port scan kare to use sirf band darwaze dikhte hain.

Rule example: ALLOW 443 from any, DENY all else inbound. Simple, par sabse zaroori — bina perimeter ke baaki layers ka koi matlab nahi.

2. Network Segmentation — andar ki deewarein

Ek baar attacker andar ghus gaya to? Agar network ek hi bada hall hai, wo kahin bhi ja sakta hai. Segmentation matlab network ko hisson me baantna: HR ka network, Finance ka alag, Production servers ka alag — har hisse ke beech firewall rules.

Example: Web server hack hua — par database segment tak sirf app server ja sakta hai, web server seedha nahi. Attacker web server pe atak gaya, database tak nahi pahuncha. Ise lateral movement rokna kehte hain.

Sahi: Har segment ke beech sirf zaroori traffic allow — 'default deny' har segment pe.

3. DMZ — beech ki safe jagah

DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) ek aisi jagah hai jo na poori bahar hai, na poori andar: public servers (website, email) yahan rehte hain. Internet se in tak pahuncha ja sakta hai, par yahan se internal network tak nahi.

Example: Web server DMZ me hai. Attacker use hack bhi kar le to internal database tak nahi ja sakta — kyunki DMZ aur internal network ke beech doosra firewall hai.

Cloud me yehi kaam public vs private subnets karte hain — public subnet me load balancer, private me database.

4. Access Control aur Content Filtering

Firewall ye bhi decide karta hai ki andar se bahar kya ja sakta hai: employees kaunse sites khol sakte hain, kaunsi application chal sakti hai. School/office me social media block karna, malware sites block karna — yahi hai.

NGFW application pehchan ke rule lagata hai: 'YouTube allow, par upload block', 'WhatsApp Web block, par WhatsApp calls allow'. Aur URL filtering se jaane-maane kharab domains block hote hain.

Saath me user-based rules bhi: Manager ko sab kuch, intern ko sirf kaam ki sites — identity se juda access control.

5. Threat Prevention (IPS) — attack ko pehchan ke roko

Modern firewall (NGFW) sirf allow/block nahi karta — wo attack ko pehchan ke rokta hai. Packet ke andar dekh ke (deep packet inspection) jaana-pehchana attack pattern mile to block + alert.

Example: SQL injection ki koshish — packet me ' OR '1'='1 dikha → IPS ne block kar diya, aur security team ko alert bhej diya. Port scan dikha → source IP ko temporarily ban kar diya.

Threat intelligence feeds se firewall ko naye attacks ki khabar milti rehti hai — jaise antivirus ko naye virus ki.

6. VPN aur Remote Access Security

Work-from-home me employee ghar se office network se judta hai — VPN ke through. Firewall VPN ka gatekeeper hai: sirf authenticated users ko andar aane do, aur unhe sirf utna dikhao jitna zaroori hai.

Example: Developer VPN se judta hai — use sirf dev servers dikhte hain, production database nahi. HR ko sirf HR systems. Ye least privilege VPN pe bhi lagta hai.

Aaj kal Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) iska modern roop hai — har user, har device, har request verify hoti hai, VPN hone se hi bharosa nahi milta.

3. 6 use cases — ek nazar me

#Use CaseKya rokta haiExample
1Perimeter protectionBahar se unauthorized accessSirf 443 khula, baaki band
2SegmentationLateral movementWeb server se DB tak seedha rasta nahi
3DMZPublic server hack → internal breachWeb server DMZ me, DB andar
4Access control / filteringGalat sites/apps, data leakMalware sites block, YouTube upload block
5Threat prevention (IPS)Known attacksSQL injection pattern block
6VPN / remote accessUnauthorized remote entryVPN + least privilege per role

4. Try karo — ek office network ko secure karo

Ek chhota office network hai: web server, database, aur employees. Har firewall use case ko ek-ek karke lagao aur dekho attack kaise rukta hai.

  1. 1. Perimeter lagao
  2. 2. Segmentation karo
  3. 3. DMZ banao
  4. 4. Content filtering lagao
  5. 5. IPS on karo
  6. 6. VPN + least privilege

5. Firewall kahan lagta hai? — placement guide

JagahKya protect karta hai
Internet edge (perimeter)Poora network, bahar se
Segments ke beechInternal lateral movement
DMZ ke dono tarafPublic servers aur internal network
Host pe (laptop/server)Us machine ko, sabse aakhri layer
Cloud (Security Groups)Virtual network, per-resource rules

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Sirf perimeter firewall pe bharosa: Andar ghusne ke baad attacker ko koi nahi rokta. Segmentation aur host firewall bhi chahiye.
  2. DMZ ko internal network samajhna: DMZ ke servers ko internal DB ka access dena matlab DMZ ka fayda khatam.
  3. Firewall rules ko kabhi review na karna: 'Temporary' rule 3 saal tak rehta hai. Har 3 mahine me rules audit karo.
  4. IPS ko 'monitor only' pe chhodna: Alert dekh ke koi action nahi — IPS ko block mode me rakho, warna ye sirf CCTV hai, guard nahi.
  5. Outgoing traffic ko ignore karna: Sirf incoming block karna kaafi nahi — malware andar se data bahar bhejta hai. Egress filtering bhi lagao.

7. Interview corner

Q: Firewall ke 6 use cases batao.

Perimeter protection, network segmentation, DMZ, access control/content filtering, threat prevention (IPS), aur VPN/remote access security. Har ek alag layer pe kaam karta hai — defense in depth.

Q: DMZ kyun zaroori hai?

DMZ public servers (web, email) ko internal network se alag rakhta hai. Public server hack bhi ho jaye to attacker internal database tak nahi pahunch sakta — beech me doosra firewall hota hai.

Q: Segmentation se kya fayda hai?

Attacker ek hisse me ghus bhi jaye to doosre hisse tak nahi ja sakta — lateral movement rukta hai. Blast radius chhota ho jata hai: ek server ka hack poora network ka hack nahi banta.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Web server hack hone par database ko kya bachata hai?

  • Perimeter firewall
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Network segmentation — DB segment tak sirf app server ja sakta hai
  • Antivirus
  • Kuch nahi

Sawaal 2: DMZ me kaunse servers rehte hain?

  • Internal database
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Public servers jaise web aur email
  • HR ke laptops
  • Backup servers
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Firewall ke 6 kaam: perimeter, segmentation, DMZ, access control, IPS aur VPN security — ek layer nahi, 6 layers mil ke defense in depth banate hain.

Firewall rules — 6 tareeke (original guide se)

Guide ke 6 firewall use cases ye hain:

  1. Port-Based Rules: Specific ports ke hisaab se traffic allow ya block karo. Example: web browsing ke liye sirf port 80 (HTTP) aur 443 (HTTPS) pe traffic allow karo.
  2. IP Address Filtering: Source ya destination IP address ke hisaab se traffic allow ya deny karo. Trusted IP addresses ko whitelist karo aur known malicious IPs ko blacklist karo.
  3. Protocol-Based Rules: Specific network protocols ke hisaab se traffic allow ya block karo — jaise TCP, UDP, ICMP. Example: sirf TCP traffic port 22 (SSH) pe allow karo.
  4. Time-Based Rules: Specific time ya schedule ke hisaab se rules enforce karo. Example: business hours me alag access rules aur after-hours me alag.
  5. Stateful Inspection: Stateful firewall active connections ki state monitor karta hai aur traffic sirf tab allow karta hai jab wo established connection se match kare — bahar se unauthorized access rukta hai.
  6. Application-Based Rules: Kuch firewalls application-level control dete hain — specific applications ya services ke hisaab se allow ya block karo. Example: Skype ya BitTorrent jaise applications ko allow ya restrict karna.
