06Security (Part 2)

Top 4 Authentication Mechanisms

'Tum kaun ho?' — ye sawaal har system poochta hai, aur iske 4 tareeke hain: kuch jo tum jaante ho, kuch jo tumhare paas hai, kuch jo tum ho, aur kuch jo tum karte ho. Is page me chaaron ko samjho — aur kaunsa kab use karna hai.

1. 4 tareeke — ghar ke darwaze ki kahani

1) Jo tum jaante ho (Knowledge): Ghar ki chabhi ka code — password ya PIN. Yaad rakhna padta hai, aur koi sun le to use bhi pata chal jayega.

2) Jo tumhare paas hai (Possession): Ghar ki asli chabhi — phone, security key, OTP. Chabhi kho gayi to andar nahi ja sakte, par chabhi chori bhi ho sakti hai.

3) Jo tum ho (Inherence): Tumhara chehra ya ungli ka nishan — fingerprint/face unlock. Chori nahi ho sakta (aasan se), par badla bhi nahi ja sakta.

4) Jo tum karte ho (Behavior): Tum kaise chalte ho, type karte ho — typing pattern, location. Background me chalta rehta hai, tumhe pata bhi nahi chalta.

Golden rule: Ek factor kaafi nahi — MFA matlab 2 alag categories milana (password + phone). Do passwords MFA nahi hain — wo ek hi category hai!

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

1. Knowledge — Password / PIN

Sabse purana aur sabse common: password, PIN, security questions. Plus: Implement karna aasan, kuch kharidna nahi padta, user samajhta hai.

Minus: Bhool jaate hain, reuse karte hain, phish ho jaate hain, brute-force hote hain. '123456' aaj bhi duniya ka sabse common password hai.

Sahi tareeka: Lamba passphrase (4 random words), password manager, breached-password check, aur kabhi bhi sirf password pe bharosa mat karo — MFA jodo.

Galat: Security questions ('tumhare pehle school ka naam?') — ye jawab social media se mil jaate hain.

2. Possession — OTP / Security Key

Tumhare paas koi cheez hai: phone pe aane wala OTP (SMS/TOTP app), hardware security key (YubiKey), ya push notification approve karna.

TOTP (Google Authenticator): Phone aur server ek secret share karte hain; har 30 second me naya 6-digit code banta hai. SMS se behtar hai — SIM swap se nahi chori hota.

Hardware key (FIDO2): Sabse strong — USB key ko chhoo ke login. Phishing-proof hai, kyunki key galat site pe kaam hi nahi karti. Google ne employees ko YubiKey di to phishing attacks zero ho gaye.

3. Inherence — Biometrics

Fingerprint, face, iris — tum jo ho. Plus: Kuch yaad nahi rakhna, fast hai, chori karna mushkil (par impossible nahi — photo se face unlock ke cases hain).

Minus: Biometric badla nahi ja sakta — fingerprint leak ho gaya to hamesha ke liye gaya. Isliye biometric device pe rehna chahiye (phone ke secure enclave me), server pe kabhi nahi.

Sahi design: Biometric sirf device unlock karta hai; server ko sirf cryptographic proof milta hai (passkeys ka model). Server pe fingerprint store karna badi galti hai.

4. Behavior — tum kaise karte ho

Typing speed, mouse movement, location, device, time — system background me dekhta rehta hai: 'Ye user hamesha Delhi se login karta hai, aaj Russia se kyun?'

Risk-based authentication: Normal behavior ho to seedha login; ajeeb behavior ho to extra step (OTP maango). Bank yehi karte hain — nayi device se login karte hi OTP aata hai.

Minus: Akela kaafi nahi — ye signal hai, proof nahi. Privacy ka sawaal bhi hai — user ko batana chahiye kya track ho raha hai.

3. MFA aur passwordless — kaunsa combination best hai?

CombinationSecurityUXKab use karo
Password only❌ Kamzor✅ AasanKabhi nahi (sensitive apps me)
Password + SMS OTP⚠ Theek⚠ TheekBasic apps (SIM swap risk hai)
Password + TOTP app✅ Achha✅ AchhaMost apps ke liye standard
Password + Hardware key✅✅ Best⚠ Key chahiyeAdmin, high-value accounts
Passkey (biometric + key)✅✅ Best✅✅ Sabse fastFuture standard

Yaad rakhna: MFA matlab alag categories — password (knowledge) + TOTP (possession). Password + security question dono knowledge hain — wo MFA nahi hai.

4. Try karo — alag-alag login try karo

Ek attacker tumhara account hack karne ki koshish kar raha hai. Dekho kaunsa authentication mechanism use rokta hai aur kaunsa nahi.

  1. 1. Sirf password — attack
  2. 2. Password + SMS OTP — attack
  3. 3. Password + TOTP app — attack
  4. 4. Password + Hardware key — attack
  5. 5. Passkey — attack

5. 4 mechanisms — ek table me

FactorExampleChori kaise hoti hai?Bachao
KnowledgePassword, PINPhishing, leak, brute forceMFA, password manager
PossessionOTP, security keySIM swap, device choriTOTP/hardware key, not SMS
InherenceFingerprint, faceSpoofing, database leakDevice pe rakho, server pe nahi
BehaviorLocation, typingMimic karna mushkilRisk signal ke roop me use karo

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Do passwords ko MFA samajhna: Password + security question dono 'knowledge' hain — MFA ke liye alag categories chahiye.
  2. SMS OTP ko safe samajhna: SIM swap attack se SMS OTP chori ho jata hai. TOTP app ya hardware key use karo.
  3. Biometric ko server pe store karna: Fingerprint leak hua to badla nahi ja sakta. Biometric hamesha device pe rehna chahiye.
  4. MFA ko sirf login pe lagana: Sensitive actions (password change, paise bhejna) pe dobara MFA maango — session hijack se bachao.
  5. Recovery ko kamzor chhodna: MFA strong hai, par 'forgot password' se bypass ho jaye to sab bekaar. Recovery flow bhi utna hi strong hona chahiye.

7. Interview corner

Q: Authentication ke 4 factors kaunse hain?

Knowledge (jo tum jaante ho — password), Possession (jo tumhare paas hai — OTP/key), Inherence (jo tum ho — fingerprint/face), Behavior (jo tum karte ho — typing/location). MFA matlab 2 alag categories milana.

Q: SMS OTP se TOTP behtar kyun hai?

SMS OTP SIM swap attack se chori ho sakta hai — attacker tumhara number apne phone pe le leta hai. TOTP code tumhare phone ke app me locally banta hai, network se nahi aata, to SIM swap se safe hai.

Q: Biometric ko server pe store kyun nahi karna chahiye?

Kyunki biometric badla nahi ja sakta — fingerprint leak hua to hamesha ke liye compromise hai. Sahi design me biometric device ke secure enclave me rehta hai aur server ko sirf cryptographic proof milta hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: MFA ka matlab kya hai?

  • Do password rakhna
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Do alag categories ke factors milana (jaise password + OTP)
  • Password bahut lamba rakhna
  • Har hafte password badalna

Sawaal 2: Sabse phishing-proof authentication kaunsa hai?

  • SMS OTP
  • Password
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Hardware security key / Passkey (FIDO2)
  • Security question
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: 4 factors: knowledge, possession, inherence, behavior; MFA = 2 alag categories; SMS OTP < TOTP < hardware key/passkey; biometric device pe rakho, server pe nahi.

Authentication ke 4 mechanisms (original guide se)

Guide ke 4 authentication mechanisms ye hain:

  1. 1. SSH Keys: Cryptographic keys se remote systems aur servers ko securely access karo.
  2. 2. OAuth Tokens: Tokens jo third-party applications ko user data ka limited access dete hain.
  3. 3. SSL Certificates: Digital certificates jo server aur client ke beech secure aur encrypted communication ensure karte hain.
  4. 4. Credentials: User authentication information (username/password) jo verify karke alag-alag systems aur services ka access grant karti hai.

Over to you (sochne wala sawaal): Tum security keys kaise manage karte ho? Kya unhe GitHub repository me rakhna achha idea hai? Jawab: nahi — secrets ko kabhi repo me mat dalo; secret manager ya environment variables use karo, aur agar galti se commit ho jaye to key ko turant revoke karke nayi key banao.

Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/top-4-forms-of-authentication-mechanisms.md
← PichhlaTop 6 Firewall Use CasesAgla →Symmetric vs Asymmetric Encryption
07Security (Part 2)

Symmetric vs Asymmetric Encryption

Encryption ke do tareeke hain — ek me ek hi chabhi se taala lagta aur khulta hai, doosre me do alag chabhiyan hoti hain. Dono ka kaam ek hai (data chhupana), par speed, key sharing aur use case bilkul alag. Ye farq samajh lo to TLS, WhatsApp aur digital signature — sab clear ho jayega.

1. Dono ko ek kahani se samjho — tijori wali kahani

Symmetric: Tumhare aur dost ke paas ek hi chabhi ki duplicate copy hai. Tum tijori band karte ho, dost wahi chabhi se kholta hai. Fast aur simple — par chabhi dost tak kaise pahunchao? Raaste me koi copy kar le to khel khatam.

Asymmetric: Dost ke paas ek khula taala (public key) hai jo wo sabko baant ta hai, aur uski chabhi (private key) sirf uske paas hai. Tum taala laga ke bhej dete ho — khol sirf dost sakta hai. Chabhi share karne ki zaroorat hi nahi — par taala lagana (encrypt karna) slow hai.

Ek line me: Symmetric = ek key, fast, par key share karna mushkil. Asymmetric = do keys, key share karna aasan, par slow. Real systems dono ko milake use karte hain (hybrid).

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Symmetric — ek key, dono taraf

Ek hi secret key se encrypt aur decrypt — AES-256 aaj ka standard hai. Bahut fast hai: gigabytes data bhi secondon me encrypt ho jata hai. Isliye bade data (files, disk, network traffic) ke liye symmetric hi use hota hai.

Problem — key distribution: Key dono taraf kaise pahunche? Agar key network pe bhejoge to attacker bhi padh lega. Isliye key ko pehle se share karna padta hai (mil ke, ya secure channel se) — jo internet pe strangers ke beech possible nahi.

Algorithms: AES (standard), ChaCha20 (mobile pe fast), DES/3DES (purane, ab mat use karo).

Asymmetric — public + private key

Do keys ka joda: public key sabko de sakte ho, private key sirf tumhare paas. Public key se encrypt karo → sirf private key khol sakti hai. Private key se sign karo → public key verify kar sakti hai.

Plus: Key share karne ki problem khatam — public key to naam ke saath hi public hai. Minus: Symmetric se 100-1000x slow — bade data encrypt karna practical nahi.

Algorithms: RSA (classic), ECC (chhoti key, same security — mobile/IoT me popular), Diffie-Hellman (key exchange ke liye).

Sahi: Asymmetric se sirf chhoti cheez encrypt karo (jaise symmetric key) — bade data ke liye nahi.

Hybrid — dono ka best combination

Real duniya me dono saath kaam karte hain — TLS handshake iska best example hai:

1) Browser aur server asymmetric crypto (ECDHE) se ek shared secret tay karte hain — key exchange safe ho gaya, bina key share kiye.

2) Us secret se symmetric session key banti hai (AES) — aur phir saara data usi se encrypt hota hai, fast.

WhatsApp, Signal, har HTTPS site — sab hybrid use karte hain. Asymmetric = taala lagane ki meeting, Symmetric = uske baad ki fast baat-cheet.

Key sizes aur security — kitni badi key?

AES-128 bhi aaj ke liye kaafi strong hai, AES-256 future-proof hai (quantum computer ke khilaf bhi zyada time tikega). RSA-2048 minimum hai, RSA-1024 ab toot chuka hai. ECC-256 lagbhag RSA-3072 ke barabar security deta hai — chhoti key, kam battery, isliye mobile pe ECC pasand hai.

Quantum ka sawaal: Quantum computer aaya to RSA/ECC toot jayenge (Shor's algorithm), par AES sirf aadha kamzor hoga (Grover's) — AES-256 tab bhi safe rahega. Isliye post-quantum crypto pe kaam chal raha hai.

Galat: 'Meri key 4096-bit hai to main safe hoon' — key size ke saath key management (storage, rotation) bhi utna hi zaroori hai.

3. Side-by-side comparison

CheezSymmetric (AES)Asymmetric (RSA/ECC)
KeysEk secret keyPublic + private key pair
Speed⚡ Bahut fast🐢 Slow (100-1000x)
Key sharingMushkil (secure channel chahiye)Aasan (public key public hai)
Best forBada data, files, disk, network trafficKey exchange, signatures, small data
Key size128/256-bitRSA 2048-bit / ECC 256-bit
ExampleAES-256, ChaCha20RSA, ECC, Diffie-Hellman
# Python — hybrid ka mini demo
from cryptography.fernet import Fernet   # symmetric (AES)
# 1) Symmetric key banao — ye fast hai
key = Fernet.generate_key()
cipher = Fernet(key)
token = cipher.encrypt(b"mera secret message")
# 2) Is key ko dost ko bhejna ho to use dost ki PUBLIC key se encrypt karo (asymmetric)
# Dost apni PRIVATE key se key nikaalega, phir message decrypt karega — hybrid!

4. Try karo — dono tareekon se message bhejo

Ek secret message dost ko bhejna hai. Pehle symmetric, phir asymmetric, phir hybrid try karo — aur dekho key share karne me kya problem aati hai.

  1. 1. Symmetric — AES se encrypt karo
  2. 2. Asymmetric — RSA se encrypt karo
  3. 3. Hybrid — TLS jaisa
  4. 4. Attacker key chura le to?

5. Kab kya use karo?

KaamUse karo
File/disk encrypt karnaSymmetric (AES-256)
Network traffic (TLS)Hybrid (ECDHE + AES)
Digital signatureAsymmetric (private key se sign)
Kisi ko secret bhejna (pehli baar)Asymmetric (uski public key se)
Password store karnaNa symmetric, na asymmetric — Hashing (bcrypt/Argon2)

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Bade data ko RSA se encrypt karna: Bahut slow hai aur size limit bhi hai. Hybrid use karo — RSA se sirf symmetric key bhejo.
  2. Symmetric key ko plain text me bhejna: Key network pe bhej di to encryption bekaar. Key exchange ke liye asymmetric ya pre-shared secure channel use karo.
  3. DES ya RSA-1024 use karna: Dono toot chuke hain. AES-128+ aur RSA-2048+ minimum hai.
  4. ECB mode use karna: AES ka ECB mode same plaintext ko same ciphertext deta hai — pattern dikh jata hai. GCM/CBC mode use karo.
  5. Key ko code me hardcode karna: Key leak hui to saara data khul jayega. KMS/vault me rakho, rotate karo.

7. Interview corner

Q: Symmetric aur asymmetric encryption me farq kya hai?

Symmetric me ek hi key se encrypt/decrypt hota hai (AES) — fast hai, par key share karna mushkil. Asymmetric me public/private key pair hota hai — key share karna aasan, par slow hai. Real systems hybrid use karte hain.

Q: TLS me dono kaise saath kaam karte hain?

Handshake me asymmetric crypto (ECDHE) se shared secret tay hota hai, phir us secret se symmetric session key (AES) banti hai jisse saara data encrypt hota hai — safe key exchange + fast bulk encryption.

Q: RSA se bada file encrypt kyun nahi karte?

Kyunki RSA symmetric se 100-1000x slow hai aur uski size limit bhi hoti hai. Bade data ke liye AES use karte hain; RSA sirf chhoti cheez (jaise AES key) ke liye.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Bade data (1GB file) ko encrypt karne ke liye kya best hai?

  • RSA
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: AES (symmetric)
  • Base64
  • MD5

Sawaal 2: Asymmetric encryption ka sabse bada fayda kya hai?

  • Ye fast hai
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Key share karna aasan — public key sabko de sakte ho
  • Isme key nahi hoti
  • Ye kabhi slow nahi hota
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Symmetric (AES) = ek key, fast, bada data; Asymmetric (RSA/ECC) = key pair, slow, key exchange + signatures; real systems hybrid use karte hain — asymmetric se key, symmetric se data.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/symmetric-encryption-vs-asymmetric-encryption.md
← PichhlaTop 4 Authentication MechanismsAgla →Session-based Authentication vs. JWT
08Security (Part 2)

Session-based Authentication vs. JWT

Login ke baad user ko pehchanne ke do sabse popular tareeke — Session-based auth aur JWT. Dono kaam karte hain, par inke trade-offs ulte hain: ek me control zyada, doosre me scale aasan. Interview me ye sawaal lagbhag pakka aata hai.

1. Dono ko ek kahani se samjho — hotel wali kahani

Session: Hotel me check-in karte ho — reception pe tumhara naam register me likha jata hai, aur tumhe ek room key card milta hai. Har baar room kholne pe guard register check karta hai: 'Room 42, Priya — theek hai.' Key kho jaye to reception turant band kar deta hai.

JWT: Is baar hotel tumhe ek card deta hai jisme sab kuch likha hai — naam, room number, check-out date — aur neeche hotel ki stamp (signature) hai. Guard card padh ke, stamp check karke jaane deta hai — register dekhne ki zaroorat nahi. Par card kho jaye to koi bhi use kar sakta hai, jab tak check-out date na aaye.

Ek line me: Session = server yaad rakhta hai (stateful). JWT = client saboot leke chalta hai (stateless). Ek me revoke aasan, doosre me scale aasan.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Session-based auth — kaise kaam karta hai?

Flow: User login karta hai → server session banata hai (user id, role — Redis/DB me) → browser ko random session ID deta hai (cookie me) → har request pe server ID se lookup karta hai → user mil gaya to allow.

Plus: Logout turant kaam karta hai (session delete), data server pe safe hai (user badal nahi sakta), session ka size chhota hai (sirf ID travel karta hai).

Minus: Har request pe DB/Redis lookup — latency aur load. Multiple servers ho to shared store chahiye (Redis). Mobile apps me cookie handle karna awkward hai.

JWT auth — kaise kaam karta hai?

Flow: User login karta hai → server JWT sign karta hai (payload: user id, role, expiry) → client use store karta hai (localStorage ya cookie) → har request pe Authorization: Bearer <token> bhejta hai → server signature verify karta hai, payload padhta hai — koi lookup nahi.

Plus: Stateless — server ko kuch yaad nahi rakhna, scale karna aasan; microservices me har service khud verify kar sakti hai; mobile apps ke liye natural hai.

Minus: Revoke mushkil — token expiry tak valid rehta hai; payload bada ho sakta hai (har request pe travel karta hai); payload decode karke padha ja sakta hai (sensitive data mat rakho).

Security — kaunsa zyada safe hai?

Session: Session ID chori hui to bhi server use turant invalid kar sakta hai. CSRF ka khatra hai (cookie automatic bhejti hai) — SameSite + CSRF token se bachao.

JWT: Token chori hua to expiry tak valid — isliye short expiry (15 min) + refresh token pattern use karo. LocalStorage me rakha to XSS se chori ho sakta hai — HttpOnly cookie behtar hai.

Refresh token pattern: Access token chhota (15 min), refresh token lamba (7 din) aur server pe store (revoke possible). Access token expire ho to client refresh token se naya maangta hai — server check karta hai refresh token abhi bhi valid hai ya revoke ho gaya.

Kaunsa kab chuno? — decision guide

Session chuno jab: Traditional web app ho, banking/high-security ho (turant revoke chahiye), ya single server/monolith ho.

JWT chuno jab: Mobile app ho, microservices ho, third-party APIs ho, ya stateless scale chahiye ho.

Dono mila ke: Kai bade apps hybrid use karte hain — JWT (short-lived) + refresh token server pe. Isse stateless ka fayda aur revoke ka control, dono milte hain.

Interview line: 'Session stateful hai — control zyada, scale mushkil. JWT stateless hai — scale aasan, revoke mushkil. Choice use case pe depend karti hai, dono me se koi universally behtar nahi.'

3. Side-by-side comparison

CheezSession-basedJWT
StateStateful (server pe)Stateless (client pe)
Data kahan?Server (Redis/DB)Token me (payload)
Har request peStore lookupSignature verify
Logout / revokeTurant ✓Mushkil — expiry ya blocklist
ScaleShared store chahiyeAasan
Mobile appsAwkward (cookie)Natural (header)
Token sizeChhota (sirf ID)Bada (payload + signature)
Main riskCSRF, session hijackToken theft, no instant revoke

4. Try karo — dono se login aur logout karo

Dono systems me login karo, phir ek attacker token/session chura leta hai. Tum logout karte ho — kaunsa system attacker ko rok pata hai?

  1. 1. Session login + logout
  2. 2. JWT login + logout
  3. 3. JWT + refresh token (sahi design)
  4. 4. Scale test — 1 lakh users

5. JWT ko sahi tareeke se use karne ke rules

RuleKyun
Short expiry (15 min)Chori hua token zyada der kaam na kare
Refresh token alag se, server pe storedRevoke ka control wapas mile
Payload me sensitive data nahiPayload koi bhi decode kar sakta hai
HttpOnly cookie (web apps)XSS se token chori na ho
Strong signing algorithm (RS256/HS256)'none' algorithm se koi bhi token bana lega
Issuer/audience check karoDoosri app ka token yahan na chale

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. JWT ko session ki tarah treat karna: 'Logout = token delete' — server ko pata hi nahi chalta. Short expiry + refresh token use karo.
  2. JWT payload me password/PII rakhna: Payload sirf Base64 hai — koi bhi padh sakta hai. Sirf user id, role, expiry rakho.
  3. JWT ko kabhi expire na karna: Lifetime token chori hone par hamesha kaam karega. Expiry zaroori hai.
  4. Signing key ko weak ya public rakhna: HS256 ki secret key leak hui to koi bhi token bana sakta hai. Key ko vault me rakho.
  5. Session ke liye JWT force karna: Simple web app me session kaafi hai — JWT ki complexity bina wajah mat lao.

7. Interview corner

Q: Session aur JWT me main farq kya hai?

Session stateful hai — server session store me user ka data rakhta hai, browser me sirf ID. JWT stateless hai — user ka data token me hi hota hai, server ko lookup nahi karna padta. Session me revoke turant, JWT me scale aasan.

Q: JWT ka logout problem kya hai?

JWT self-contained hota hai — server ko pata nahi chalta ki user ne logout kiya. Token expiry tak valid rehta hai. Fix: short expiry (15 min) + server pe stored refresh token, jise logout pe revoke kar sakte ho.

Q: Kab session, kab JWT use karoge?

Web app/banking jahan turant revoke chahiye → session. Mobile app/microservices/API jahan stateless scale chahiye → JWT. Kai apps hybrid use karte hain: short-lived JWT + refresh token.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: JWT stateless kyun hai?

  • Isme password nahi hota
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Server ko verify ke liye session store lookup nahi karna padta
  • Ye cookie me nahi rehta
  • Ye chhota hota hai

Sawaal 2: JWT me turant logout kyun mushkil hai?

  • Token client pe hota hai
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Server ko pata nahi chalta — token expiry tak valid rehta hai
  • Password badal jata hai
  • Browser token delete nahi karta
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Session = stateful, revoke turant, scale mushkil; JWT = stateless, scale aasan, revoke mushkil; best practice: short-lived JWT + server-stored refresh token; use case dekh ke chuno.

Dono flows — step by step (original guide se)

Flight ticket wali analogy se samjho: Session-based me tumhe sirf Ticket ID milti hai — baaki saari details airline ke database me rehti hain. JWT-based me tumhe poori ticket hi mil jati hai, saari details usi pe encoded hoti hain.

Session-Based Authentication — kaise kaam karta hai:

  1. User login request karta hai aur frontend app request ko backend server ko bhejti hai.
  2. Backend secret key se session banata hai aur data ko session storage me store karta hai.
  3. Server client ko cookie me unique session ID bhejta hai.
  4. User nayi request karta hai aur browser request ke saath session ID bhejta hai.
  5. Server session ID se user ko authenticate karta hai.

JWT-Based Authentication — kaise kaam karta hai:

  1. User login request karta hai aur request backend server pe jati hai.
  2. Server credentials verify karke JWT issue karta hai. JWT private key se sign hota hai aur koi session storage involved nahi hota.
  3. JWT client ko cookie ya response body me bheja jata hai. Dono tareekon ke apne fayde aur nuksaan hain, par yahan cookie wala tareeka use kiya gaya hai.
  4. Har aage wali request pe browser cookie ke saath JWT bhejta hai.
  5. Server secret private key se JWT verify karta hai aur user info nikaalta hai.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/what's-the-difference-between-session-based-authentication-and-jwts.md
← PichhlaSymmetric vs Asymmetric EncryptionAgla →JWT 101: Key to Stateless Authentication
09Security (Part 2)

JWT 101: Key to Stateless Authentication

JWT (JSON Web Token) aaj ki APIs ki pehchan hai — har request me ek token, server ko kuch yaad nahi rakhna padta. Par JWT kya hai, iske teen hisse kya karte hain, aur isse galat use karne par kya hota hai — ye sab is page me.

1. JWT — stamp wala ID card

Socho ek mela hai. Entry pe tumhe ek card milta hai jisme likha hai: naam, ticket type (VIP/Normal), aur expiry time — aur neeche organizer ki mohar (stamp) hai. Har ride pe guard card padh ke, mohar check karke andar jaane deta hai — use entry register dekhne ki zaroorat nahi.

JWT wahi card hai: Header (kaunsa algorithm), Payload (tum kaun ho, kya kar sakte ho, kab tak valid hai), Signature (server ki mohar — koi badal nahi sakta). Guard (server) sirf mohar verify karta hai.

Yaad rakhna: JWT ka payload encrypted nahi hota — sirf Base64 encoded hota hai. Koi bhi padh sakta hai. Mohar sirf ye kehti hai ki 'ye card asli hai, badla nahi gaya'.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Teen hisse — Header, Payload, Signature

Header: Token ka type (JWT) aur signing algorithm (HS256 ya RS256). {"alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT"}

Payload (Claims): User ki info — sub (user id), name, role, iat (issued at), exp (expiry). Standard claims ke alawa custom claims bhi daal sakte ho.

Signature: HMACSHA256(base64(header) + "." + base64(payload), secret) — secret key sirf server ke paas hoti hai. Payload me ek letter bhi badla to signature match nahi karega.

Teeno hisse dot (.) se jude hote hain: xxxxx.yyyyy.zzzzz

JWT kaise banta aur verify hota hai?

Banana (login ke waqt): User login karta hai → server payload banata hai (user id, role, expiry 15 min) → secret key se sign karta hai → token client ko deta hai.

Verify (har request pe): Client Authorization: Bearer <token> bhejta hai → server signature dobara compute karta hai → match hua to token asli hai → expiry check karta hai → payload se user nikaalta hai. Koi DB lookup nahi — isliye stateless.

HS256 vs RS256: HS256 me ek hi secret key sign aur verify dono karti hai (server ke andar). RS256 me private key sign karti hai, public key verify karti hai — microservices me har service public key se verify kar sakti hai, secret share kiye bina.

Access token + Refresh token — poora pattern

Access token ko chhota rakho (15 min) — chori bhi ho to zyada nuksaan nahi. Refresh token ko lamba rakho (7-30 din) aur server pe store karo (DB me, revoke possible).

Flow: Access token expire → client refresh token bhejta hai → server check karta hai (valid hai? revoke to nahi hua?) → naya access token deta hai. Logout = refresh token delete (server pe) + access token 15 min me khud expire.

Refresh token rotation: Har baar naya refresh token do, purana invalid kar do. Agar purana refresh token dobara use hua to samjho token chori hua hai — saare tokens revoke kar do.

JWT kahan store karo?

LocalStorage: JS padh sakta hai — XSS attack se token chori ho sakta hai. Aasan hai, par risky.

HttpOnly Cookie: JS padh nahi sakta — XSS se safe. Par CSRF ka khatra — SameSite + CSRF token chahiye. Web apps ke liye best.

Memory (JS variable): Sabse safe (XSS se bhi mushkil), par page refresh hote hi gayab — refresh token se dobara lena padta hai. High-security SPAs me ye pattern popular hai.

Sahi: Web app → HttpOnly cookie + SameSite. Mobile app → secure storage (Keychain/Keystore).

3. JWT ko decode karo — khud dekho

# Ek asli JWT — jwt.io pe paste karke dekho
eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.
eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IlByaXlhIiwicm9sZSI6InVzZXIiLCJpYXQiOjE1MTYyMzkwMjIsImV4cCI6MTUxNjIzOTkyMn0.
SflKxwRJSMeKKF2QT4fwpMeJf36POk6yJV_adQssw5c
HEADER  (decode): {"alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT"}
PAYLOAD (decode): {"sub": "1234567890", "name": "Priya",
                   "role": "user", "iat": 1516239022, "exp": 1516239922}
SIGNATURE: sirf secret key se verify hoti hai — tum decode kar sakte ho,
           par bana nahi sakte (bina secret ke)!

Try karo: Upar wala token jwt.io pe paste karo — payload saaf dikhega. Yahi saboot hai ki payload me sensitive data kabhi mat rakho.

4. Try karo — JWT banao, badlo, verify karo

Ek JWT banao, use decode karo, phir payload badal ke dekho — signature kya kehta hai? Aur expiry ka kya hota hai?

  1. 1. Login karo — JWT pao
  2. 2. Token decode karo (koi key nahi chahiye)
  3. 3. Payload badlo — role=user → admin
  4. 4. Expired token bhejo
  5. 5. 'none' algorithm attack (purana bug)

5. JWT claims — standard fields

ClaimMatlab
subSubject — user ki ID
issIssuer — kisne token diya
audAudience — kis app ke liye hai
expExpiry time
iatIssued at
nbfNot before — is time se pehle valid nahi
jtiJWT ID — unique, revoke/blocklist ke liye

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Payload me sensitive data rakhna: Payload sirf Base64 hai — koi bhi decode kar sakta hai. Password, phone, card kabhi nahi.
  2. Bina expiry ke token banana: Lifetime token chori hone par hamesha kaam karega. Hamesha exp set karo, chhota rakho.
  3. Secret key ko weak ya public rakhna: 'secret123' se sign kiya to koi bhi token bana lega. Lambi random key, vault me rakho.
  4. Algorithm ko token se lene dena: Attacker alg=none bhej sakta hai. Server hamesha apna expected algorithm enforce kare.
  5. LocalStorage me token rakhna (web apps): XSS hote hi token chori. HttpOnly cookie ya memory storage behtar hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: JWT ke teen hisse kaunse hain?

Header (algorithm + type), Payload (claims — user id, role, expiry), Signature (header + payload ka HMAC, secret key se). Teenon dot se jude hote hain. Signature verify karke server token ki authenticity check karta hai.

Q: JWT stateless kyun hai?

Kyunki verify ke liye server ko session store lookup nahi karna padta — signature verify karo, payload padho, ho gaya. Isliye JWT microservices aur APIs me scale karna aasan hai.

Q: JWT revoke kaise karte ho?

Seedha revoke nahi hota — isliye short expiry + refresh token pattern use karte hain. Refresh token server pe store hota hai, use logout pe delete kar sakte ho. Ya blocklist (jti) maintain karo — par wo stateless nature ko kam karta hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: JWT ka payload kya hota hai?

  • Encrypted data jo koi nahi padh sakta
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Base64 encoded data — koi bhi decode karke padh sakta hai
  • Password ka hash
  • Server ka address

Sawaal 2: JWT me signature kis cheez se banti hai?

  • User ke password se
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Server ki secret/private key se
  • Browser se
  • Kisi key se nahi
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: JWT = Header.Payload.Signature; payload padha ja sakta hai, signature badli nahi ja sakti; stateless = scale aasan; short expiry + refresh token se revoke ka control rakho.

JWT sign karne ke 2 tareeke (original guide se)

JWT ke 3 main hisse hote hain: Header — JWT ko sign karne wale algorithms batata hai, JSON format me likha hota hai. Payload — claims aur user data hota hai; claims registered, public aur private types ke hote hain. Signature — JWT ko secure banati hai; ye encoded header, encoded payload, secret key aur algorithm ko sign karke banti hai.

JWT ko 2 tareekon se sign kiya ja sakta hai:

  • Symmetric Signatures: Sign karne aur verify karne ke liye ek hi secret key use hoti hai. Wahi key JWT sign karne wale server aur verify karne wale system — dono ke paas honi chahiye.
  • Asymmetric Signatures: Sign karne ke liye private key aur verify karne ke liye public key use hoti hai. Private key server pe safe rehti hai, jabki public key kisi ko bhi di ja sakti hai jo token verify karna chahta hai.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/jwt-101-key-to-stateless-authentication.md
← PichhlaSession-based Authentication vs. JWTAgla →Is HTTPS Safe?
10Security (Part 2)

Is HTTPS Safe?

Browser me taala dikh raha hai — matlab site safe hai? Nahi, bilkul nahi. HTTPS sirf connection ko secure karta hai, site ko trustworthy nahi banata. Is page me samjho HTTPS kya-kya bachata hai, aur kya-kya nahi bachata.

1. HTTPS — band lifafe wali kahani

Socho tum ek letter bhej rahe ho. HTTP matlab postcard — raaste me koi bhi padh sakta hai. HTTPS matlab band lifafa — andar kya likha hai, koi nahi padh sakta, aur lifafa khula to pata chal jata hai.

Par lifafa ye nahi batata ki paane wala kaun hai — agar tumne galat address pe bhej diya to lifafa usi galat aadmi ko milega, poora band hua. Isi tarah HTTPS tumhara data raaste me bachata hai, par agar site khud fake hai to tumhara data fake site ko hi milega — encrypted hoke!

Ek line me: HTTPS = raasta safe hai. Site safe hai ya nahi — ye alag sawaal hai, jiska jawab domain aur certificate deta hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

HTTPS kya bachata hai?

1) Eavesdropping: Wi-Fi pe baitha attacker tumhara password ya card number nahi padh sakta — sab encrypted hai.

2) Tampering: Beech me koi data badal nahi sakta — MAC/integrity check fail ho jayega.

3) Pehchan (kuch had tak): Certificate batata hai ki site ka domain wahi hai jo tumne khola — par certificate lena aasan hai, koi bhi le sakta hai.

Ye teeno mil ke confidentiality + integrity + authentication dete hain — connection ke level pe.

HTTPS kya NAHI bachata?

1) Phishing: Fake site goggle.com bhi HTTPS use kar sakti hai — free certificate 2 minute me milta hai. Taala dekh ke bharosa mat karo, domain dekho.

2) Malware: HTTPS site se download kiya file virus bhi ho sakta hai — encryption file ko safe nahi banata.

3) Server ki security: Site ka server hack ho to tumhara data server pe leak hoga — HTTPS sirf raaste ko bachata hai, server ko nahi.

4) Privacy (poori): ISP ko pata chal jata hai tum kis domain pe gaye (SNI/DNS se) — sirf andar ka content chhupa rehta hai.

Certificate — kaun deta hai, kaise check karein?

Certificate Certificate Authority (CA) deta hai — Let's Encrypt (free), DigiCert, Google Trust Services. Browser ke paas trusted CAs ki list hoti hai.

DV (Domain Validation): Sirf ye check hota hai ki domain tumhara hai — 2 minute me milta hai, phishing sites bhi le leti hain. OV/EV: Company ki pehchan bhi verify hoti hai — zyada time aur paise lagte hain, par aaj kal browser EV ka naam bhi nahi dikhata.

Check kaise karo: Taale pe click karo — certificate kis ko issue hua, kab expire hoga, kis CA ne diya. Domain ko dhyaan se padho: google.com vs google-secure-login.com.

HTTPS ko aur strong kaise banao?

HSTS: Browser ko bolo 'mujhe hamesha HTTPS pe kholo' — downgrade attack rukta hai. Certificate Transparency: Har certificate public log me aata hai — koi chhup ke fake certificate nahi bana sakta.

TLS 1.3: Latest version — fast aur zyada secure, purane kamzor algorithms hataye gaye. Certificate pinning: App sirf ek specific certificate ko maane — banking apps ye karti hain.

DNS over HTTPS (DoH): DNS queries bhi encrypt karo — warna ISP ko pata chal jata hai tum kaunsi site khol rahe ho.

3. HTTPS safe hai ya nahi? — final jawab

SawaalJawab
Kya mera password raaste me safe hai?✅ Haan — encrypted hai
Kya koi beech me data badal sakta hai?❌ Nahi — integrity check hai
Kya site asli hai?⚠ Sirf domain tak — certificate DV ho sakta hai
Kya site trustworthy hai?❌ Ye HTTPS nahi batata — domain aur reputation dekho
Kya ISP ko pata chalega main kahan gaya?⚠ Domain pata chal sakta hai (DNS/SNI)
Kya download kiya file safe hai?❌ Nahi — HTTPS file ko scan nahi karta

Final jawab: HTTPS zaroori hai, par kaafi nahi. Ye connection ko secure karta hai — site ki neeyat ko nahi. Taala + sahi domain + samajhdari, teeno chahiye.

4. Try karo — kaunsi site safe hai?

4 sites dikh rahi hain. Har ek ko check karo — taala hai ya nahi, domain sahi hai ya nahi — aur decide karo: login karna safe hai ya nahi?

  1. 1. https://google.com 🔒
  2. 2. http://mybank-login.com ⚠
  3. 3. https://goggle.com 🔒 (dhyaan se!)
  4. 4. https://your-bank.com — warning ⚠
  5. 5. https://bank.com — sab theek, par...?

5. HTTP vs HTTPS — ek table me

CheezHTTPHTTPS
Encryption❌ Nahi✅ TLS se
Port80443
Data padh sakta hai?Koi bhi (network pe)Koi nahi (beech me)
CertificateNahi chahiyeChahiye (CA se)
SEO rankingKamGoogle prefer karta hai
Phishing se bachao?NahiNahi! (fake site bhi HTTPS use karti hai)

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Taala dekh ke site ko trustworthy maan lena: Phishing sites bhi HTTPS use karti hain. Domain hamesha padho.
  2. Browser warning ignore karna: Certificate warning aaye to aage mat badho — ye MITM attack ka signal ho sakta hai.
  3. HTTP site pe password dalna: Plain text me jata hai. 'Bas ek baar' bhi kaafi hai leak ke liye.
  4. HTTPS ko poori security samajhna: Ye sirf transit ki security hai. Server security, password strength aur phishing se alag se bachna padta hai.
  5. Mixed content ignore karna: HTTPS page pe HTTP se image/script load ho raha ho to attacker use badal sakta hai. Sab kuch HTTPS pe hona chahiye.

7. Interview corner

Q: Is HTTPS safe?

HTTPS connection ko safe karta hai — data encrypted rehta hai, tamper nahi ho sakta, aur certificate se domain verify hota hai. Par ye site ko trustworthy nahi banata — phishing site bhi HTTPS use kar sakti hai. Taala + sahi domain, dono check karo.

Q: HTTPS kya-kya protect karta hai?

Confidentiality (encryption se), Integrity (MAC se — beech me data badla nahi ja sakta), aur Authentication (certificate se domain verify hota hai). Ye teeno connection level pe hain.

Q: Certificate warning aaye to kya karna chahiye?

Aage mat badho. Warning ka matlab hai certificate invalid/expired hai ya domain match nahi kar raha — ye MITM attack ka signal ho sakta hai. Sahi site pe warning nahi aati.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: HTTPS hone ka matlab kya hai?

  • Site 100% trustworthy hai
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Tumhara connection encrypted hai — beech me koi padh/badal nahi sakta
  • Site kabhi hack nahi hogi
  • Koi phishing nahi ho sakti

Sawaal 2: Phishing site HTTPS kyun use kar sakti hai?

  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Certificate free aur aasan se milta hai — ye site ki neeyat nahi batata
  • Google use allow karta hai
  • Taala matlab site verified hai
  • HTTPS hack nahi ho sakta
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: HTTPS = connection safe (encryption + integrity + domain verify); site trustworthy hai ya nahi — ye HTTPS nahi batata; domain padho, warning ignore mat karo, HTTP pe password kabhi mat dalo.

Packets hijack kaise hote hain — How Packets are Hijacked (original guide se)

Agar HTTPS safe hai, to Fiddler jaise tools HTTPS se bheje gaye network packets ko kaise capture kar lete hain? Neeche wala scenario dikhata hai ki kaise ek malicious intermediate packets ko hijack karta hai. Prerequisite: intermediate server ka root certificate client ke trust-store me hona chahiye.

  1. Step 1: Client TCP connection establish karne ki request karta hai. Request maliciously intermediate server ki taraf route ho jati hai (asli backend server ki jagah). Phir client aur intermediate server ke beech TCP connection banta hai.
  2. Step 2: Intermediate server asli server se TCP connection banata hai.
  3. Step 3: Intermediate server client ko apna SSL certificate bhejta hai. Certificate me public key, hostname, expiry dates, etc. hote hain. Client certificate ko validate karta hai.
  4. Step 4: Asli server intermediate server ko apna certificate bhejta hai. Intermediate server use validate karta hai.
  5. Step 5: Client session key generate karta hai aur use intermediate server ke public key se encrypt karta hai. Intermediate server apni private key se encrypted session key ko decrypt karta hai.
  6. Step 6: Intermediate server session key ko asli server ke public key se encrypt karke wahan bhejta hai. Asli server apni private key se session key ko decrypt karta hai.
  7. Steps 7 aur 8: Ab client aur server session key (symmetric encryption) se communicate kar sakte hain. Encrypted data secure bi-directional channel me transmit hota hai. Par intermediate server hamesha data ko decrypt kar sakta hai.

Yehi wajah hai ki root certificate ko trust-store me daalna itna khatarnak hai — jo bhi us certificate ko control karta hai, wo tumhare HTTPS traffic ko padh sakta hai.

Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/is-https-safe.md

11Security (Part 2)

Types of VPNs

Saare VPN ek jaise nahi hote — ek VPN tumhe office se jodta hai, doosra tumhe Netflix ka doosre desh ka content dikhata hai, teesra do offices ko jodta hai. VPN ke 4 main types hain, aur har ek ka kaam, user aur setup alag hai. Galat type chunna matlab paise aur time, dono barbaad.

TypeKaam
🏠 User (ghar)Remote Access VPN → Office
🏢 Office ↔ OfficeSite-to-Site VPN (IPsec)
☁️ Cloud VPCCloud VPN → AWS/Azure
🌍 InternetPersonal VPN (privacy)

Repo ka original diagram (0404-vpns.png) ab 404 deta hai, isliye upar wali table wahi 4 VPN types dikhati hai.

1. VPN ke types — raaste ki kahani

Remote Access VPN: Tum ghar se office ja rahe ho — ek private raasta jo sirf tumhe office tak le jata hai. Site-to-Site VPN: Do offices ke beech ek permanent private highway — Delhi office aur Mumbai office hamesha jude hain. Personal/Commercial VPN: Tum ek taxi (VPN provider) lete ho jo tumhe kahin bhi le jata hai — par taxi wale ko pata hai tum kahan gaye. Cloud VPN: Tumhara office hi cloud me hai — VPN tumhe cloud ke private network se jodta hai.

Ek line me: Kaun kisse jud raha hai — yehi type decide karta hai: user→office, office→office, user→internet, ya user→cloud.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

1. Remote Access VPN — ghar se office

Employee apne laptop/phone se company network se judta hai — kahin se bhi. Company ka VPN server (gateway) user ko authenticate karta hai (username + MFA + certificate), phir encrypted tunnel banata hai.

Use: Work-from-home, travelling employees, contractors. Access: Sirf utna jitna role allow kare — developer ko dev servers, HR ko HR systems (least privilege).

Example: Tum ghar se VPN on karte ho → ab tum office network ke andar ho → internal tools (Jira, internal wiki, file server) khulne lagte hain jo internet se band hain.

2. Site-to-Site VPN — office se office

Do (ya zyada) offices ke networks ko permanent encrypted tunnel se jodna. Har office ke edge pe ek VPN gateway (router/firewall) hota hai — users ko kuch karna nahi padta, tunnel hamesha on rehta hai.

Use: Delhi office ka employee Mumbai office ke server ko aise access karta hai jaise wo paas me ho. Protocols: IPsec — site-to-site ka standard.

Intranet vs Extranet: Intranet = apni company ke offices. Extranet = partner/supplier company ke saath — limited access ke saath.

3. Personal / Commercial VPN — privacy ke liye

NordVPN, ProtonVPN, Surfshark jaise services — tum inke server se judte ho, phir internet pe jate ho. Kaam: public Wi-Fi pe safety, ISP se privacy, geo-blocked content.

Kaise chunein: No-log policy (audit hui ho), kill switch, DNS leak protection, WireGuard/OpenVPN support, aur apna server infrastructure (rented servers pe bharosa kam). Free se bacho — free VPN data bechta hai.

Limit: Ye tumhe anonymity nahi deta — provider tumhara traffic dekh sakta hai. Aur login karke use karoge to sites tumhe pehchan legi.

4. Cloud VPN — office cloud me hai

Company ka infrastructure AWS/Azure/GCP me hai — VPN tumhe cloud ke private network (VPC) se jodta hai. AWS Client VPN, Azure VPN Gateway jaise managed services — server maintain karne ki zaroorat nahi.

Hybrid cloud: Office network + cloud VPC ke beech site-to-site VPN — dono ek hi private network jaise kaam karte hain.

Modern alternative — ZTNA: 'Zero Trust Network Access' — VPN ki jagah har app ke liye alag, verified access. VPN poora network khol deta hai; ZTNA sirf wahi app kholta hai jo chahiye. Google (BeyondCorp) aur Cloudflare Access yehi karte hain.

3. 4 types — ek table me

TypeKaun judta haiExampleProtocol
Remote AccessUser → Office networkGhar se office toolsOpenVPN, WireGuard, IKEv2
Site-to-SiteOffice → OfficeDelhi ↔ Mumbai officeIPsec
Personal/CommercialUser → Internet (VPN server se)Wi-Fi safety, geo-contentWireGuard, OpenVPN
Cloud VPNUser/Office → Cloud VPCAWS VPC accessAWS Client VPN, IPsec
TypeKaam
🏠 Ghar / UserRemote Access VPN
🏢 OfficeSite-to-Site VPN
☁️ Cloud VPCCloud VPN
🌍 InternetPersonal VPN

Repo ka original diagram (0404-vpns.png) ab 404 deta hai, isliye upar wali table wahi 4 VPN types dikhati hai.

4. Try karo — sahi VPN chuno

4 alag situations hain. Har ek ke liye sahi VPN type chuno — galat chunoge to ya to kaam nahi hoga, ya paise barbaad honge.

  1. 1. Ghar se office ka internal tool kholna hai
  2. 2. Delhi aur Mumbai office jodne hain
  3. 3. Cafe Wi-Fi pe safe rehna hai
  4. 4. AWS VPC ka private server access karna hai
  5. 5. Sirf ek app ko access dena hai (ZTNA)

5. VPN protocols — kaunsa kab?

ProtocolSpeedSecurityBest for
WireGuard⚡ Fast✅ StrongPersonal + remote access (naya standard)
OpenVPN⚠ Medium✅ StrongHar jagah support, battle-tested
IKEv2/IPsec✅ Fast✅ StrongMobile, site-to-site
L2TP/IPsec⚠ Medium⚠ TheekOld devices
PPTPFast❌ Toota huaKabhi mat use karo

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Personal VPN se office access karne ki koshish: NordVPN tumhe office network se nahi jodta — uske liye company ka remote access VPN chahiye.
  2. Free VPN pe bharosa: Free VPN data bechta hai. No-log audited provider chuno.
  3. Site-to-site ke liye personal VPN use karna: Offices ko permanent network-level tunnel chahiye, user-level app nahi.
  4. VPN ko poori security samajhna: VPN sirf transport secure karta hai — phishing, malware aur weak passwords se nahi bachata.
  5. PPTP use karna: PPTP toot chuka hai — kabhi mat use karo. WireGuard ya OpenVPN lo.

7. Interview corner

Q: VPN ke main types kaunse hain?

Remote Access (user→office), Site-to-Site (office→office, IPsec), Personal/Commercial (user→internet, privacy), aur Cloud VPN (user→cloud VPC). Har ek ka user aur use case alag hai.

Q: Remote Access aur Site-to-Site VPN me farq?

Remote Access me individual user apne device se office network se judta hai (on-demand). Site-to-Site me do networks ke gateways ke beech permanent tunnel hota hai — users ko kuch karna nahi padta, poora network juda rehta hai.

Q: ZTNA VPN se behtar kyun kaha jata hai?

VPN judne ke baad poora network khol deta hai — attacker andar ghus gaya to kahin bhi ja sakta hai. ZTNA har app ke liye alag, identity-verified access deta hai — least privilege. Isliye modern companies VPN se ZTNA ki taraf ja rahi hain.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Ghar se office ka internal tool kholne ke liye kaunsa VPN chahiye?

  • Personal VPN (NordVPN)
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Remote Access VPN (company ka)
  • Site-to-Site VPN
  • Koi VPN nahi

Sawaal 2: Do offices ko permanently jodne ke liye kaunsa VPN use hota hai?

  • Remote Access VPN
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Site-to-Site VPN (IPsec)
  • Personal VPN
  • Cloud VPN
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: 4 types: Remote Access (user→office), Site-to-Site (office→office), Personal (user→internet, privacy), Cloud VPN (user→VPC); use case dekh ke chuno; ZTNA VPN ka modern, least-privilege replacement hai.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/types-of-vpns.md
← PichhlaIs HTTPS Safe?Agla →What is a Cookie?
12Security (Part 2)

What is a Cookie?

Har website tumse kehti hai 'Accept cookies?' — par cookie hoti kya hai? Ye koi khane ki cheez nahi, ye ek chhota sa text note hai jo website tumhare browser me chhod jati hai, taaki wo tumhe dobara pehchan sake. Is page me cookie ko bilkul shuruaat se samjho.

1. Cookie — library card wali kahani

Socho tum ek library jaate ho. Pehli baar tum apna naam likhwate ho, aur library tumhe ek card deti hai. Agli baar tum card dikhate ho — librarian ko tumhara naam, tumne kaunsi kitabein li hain, sab yaad aa jata hai. Tumhe dobara naam batane ki zaroorat nahi.

Cookie wahi card hai: website tumhe ek chhota sa note deti hai (browser me save hota hai), aur tum har baar use leke aate ho. Website note padh ke kehti hai: 'Arre, ye to Priya hai — iska dark mode on hai, iske cart me 3 cheezein hain!'

Ek line me: Cookie = website ka browser me chhoda hua chhota sa yaad-dasht wala note. HTTP stateless hai — cookie hi use 'yaad' dilati hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Cookie hoti kya hai?

Cookie ek chhota text file hai (max ~4KB) jo server browser ko deta hai aur browser store karke rakhta hai. Har cookie me hota hai: naam, value, domain, path, expiry.

Example: theme=dark — naam 'theme', value 'dark'. Ya session_id=abc123 — login ki pehchan.

Browser har baar jab usi domain ko request bhejta hai to cookie ko saath bhej deta hai — automatic, tumhe kuch karna nahi padta. Isi se website tumhe pehchanti hai.

Cookie banti aur kaam kaise karti hai?

Step 1: Tum pehli baar site kholte ho. Step 2: Server response me bhejta hai: Set-Cookie: theme=dark; Max-Age=2592000. Step 3: Browser cookie ko save kar leta hai. Step 4: Agli baar request me browser bhejta hai: Cookie: theme=dark. Step 5: Server padh ke dark mode dikhata hai.

Cookie ki expiry hoti hai — session cookie browser band hote hi delete ho jati hai, persistent cookie expiry date tak rehti hai (jaise 30 din).

Cookie ke types

Session cookie: Browser band hote hi khatam — login session ke liye. Persistent cookie: Expiry tak rehti hai — 'Remember me' ke liye.

First-party cookie: Usi site ki jo tum khole ho — login, theme, cart. Third-party cookie: Doosri site ki — ads aur tracking ke liye (jaise Facebook ka button jo har site pe hai, wo tumhe track karta hai). Browsers ab third-party cookies ko block kar rahe hain (Chrome, Safari, Firefox).

Secure cookie: Sirf HTTPS pe bheji jati hai. HttpOnly cookie: JavaScript use padh nahi sakta — security ke liye.

Cookie safe hai ya khatarnak?

Cookie khud khatarnak nahi hai — ye sirf text hai, virus nahi chala sakti. Khatra is baat me hai ki usme kya rakha hai aur kaun use padh sakta hai.

Safe: Theme, language, session ID (HttpOnly + Secure flags ke saath). Khatarnak: Cookie me password ya sensitive data rakhna; third-party tracking cookies jo tumhari browsing history banati hain.

GDPR: Europe me tracking cookies ke liye tumhari permission chahiye — isliye 'Accept cookies?' banner dikhta hai. Zaroori cookies (login) ke liye permission nahi chahiye.

Sahi: Browser settings me third-party cookies block karo, aur waqt-waqt pe cookies clear karo.

3. Cookie ko browser me dekho

# Browser me cookie dekhna (Chrome DevTools):
# F12 → Application tab → Cookies → site chuno
# Tumhe dikhega: Name | Value | Domain | Path | Expires | HttpOnly | Secure
# JavaScript se cookie padhna (sirf non-HttpOnly wali):
document.cookie
// "theme=dark; lang=en"
// HttpOnly cookies yahan NAHI dikhengi — wahi to unki security hai!

Cookie delete kaise karein? Browser settings → Privacy → Clear cookies. Ya site logout kare to server cookie ko expire kar deta hai (Max-Age=0).

4. Try karo — ek din cookies ke saath

Ek shopping site pe jao: login karo, theme badlo, cart me cheez daalo — aur dekho cookies kya-kya yaad rakhti hain. Phir cookies clear karo — kya hota hai?

  1. 1. Pehli visit — site kholo
  2. 2. Dark mode chuno
  3. 3. Cart me cheez daalo
  4. 4. Doosri site pe tracking cookie
  5. 5. Cookies clear karo

5. Cookie ke baare me quick facts

CheezFact
Size~4KB per cookie, ~20 per domain
Har request pe jati hai?Haan — automatic
Virus chala sakti hai?Nahi — sirf text hai
JavaScript padh sakta hai?Sirf non-HttpOnly wali
Third-party cookiesTracking ke liye — browsers block kar rahe hain
Consent (GDPR)Tracking cookies ke liye zaroori

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Har cookie ko 'Accept' kar dena: Tracking cookies ko reject karo — 'Reject all' ya 'Only necessary' chuno.
  2. Cookie me sensitive data rakhna: Password ya card number cookie me kabhi nahi — server pe rakho.
  3. Cookie ko virus samajhna: Cookie code nahi chala sakti — par tracking aur session hijack ka risk hai, isliye flags zaroori hain.
  4. Public computer pe 'Remember me' on karna: Persistent cookie us computer pe reh jayegi — agla user tumhare account me ghus sakta hai.
  5. Cookie flags ignore karna (developers): Auth cookie pe HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite lagana zaroori hai — warna XSS aur CSRF se chori hogi.

7. Interview corner

Q: Cookie kya hai?

Cookie ek chhota text file hai jo server browser ko deta hai (Set-Cookie header se) aur browser store karke har request me wapas bhejta hai (Cookie header se). Isse stateless HTTP me bhi website user ko pehchan sakti hai — login, theme, cart jaise kaam ke liye.

Q: First-party aur third-party cookie me farq?

First-party cookie usi site ki hoti hai jo tum khole ho (login, preferences). Third-party cookie doosri site ki hoti hai — jaise ads/tracking scripts jo tumhari browsing ko cross-site track karte hain. Browsers ab third-party cookies block kar rahe hain.

Q: Cookie virus hai?

Nahi — cookie sirf text hai, code execute nahi kar sakti. Khatra isme hai ki usme sensitive data ho ya use track karne ke liye use kiya jaye. HttpOnly, Secure aur SameSite flags se cookie ko secure kiya jata hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Cookie ka main kaam kya hai?

  • Virus phailana
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Website ko user ko pehchanne aur yaad rakhne me madad karna
  • Internet ko fast banana
  • Password crack karna

Sawaal 2: Third-party cookie kis kaam aati hai?

  • Login karne ke
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Doosri sites par user ko track karne ke (ads/analytics)
  • Theme save karne ke
  • Password store karne ke
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Cookie = server ka browser me chhoda chhota text note; Set-Cookie se banti hai, Cookie header se wapas jati hai; first-party (login/theme) useful, third-party (tracking) ko block karo; auth cookie pe HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite lagao.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/what-is-a-cookie.md
