13Security (Part 2)

OAuth 2.0 Flows

'Login with Google' dabate ho, ya kisi app ko apne Drive ki permission dete ho — peeche OAuth 2.0 chalta hai. Par OAuth ke 4 alag flows hain, aur galat flow chunna matlab security hole. Is page me har flow ko kab aur kyun use karna hai, samjho.

1. OAuth flows — chaabi dene ke 4 tareeke

Socho tum apne ghar ki chaabi kisi ko dena chahte ho: (1) Authorization Code: Tum khud jaake guard ko kehte ho 'is aadmi ko andar jaane do' — guard use ek slip deta hai, wo slip dikha ke andar jata hai. Sabse safe. (2) Implicit: Tum seedha chaabi uske haath me de dete ho — fast, par koi beech me chheen sakta hai (purana, ab band). (3) Client Credentials: Do machines aapas me baat kar rahi hain — koi insaan nahi, dono ke paas apni ID hai. (4) Device Code: Tumhare TV pe code aata hai, tum phone se approve karte ho — TV pe type karna mushkil hai, isliye.

Yaad rakhna: OAuth authorization hai (kya kar sakte ho), authentication nahi (tum kaun ho — uske liye OIDC). Har flow ek alag situation ke liye bana hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

1. Authorization Code Flow — sabse common aur safe

Kab: Web apps (server wali) aur mobile apps — aaj ka standard. Kaise: (1) App tumhe authorization server (Google) pe bhejti hai. (2) Tum login + consent dete ho. (3) Google app ko ek authorization code deta hai (URL me, 10 min valid). (4) App apne server se code + client secret bhej ke access token leti hai. (5) Token se API call hoti hai.

PKCE: Mobile/public clients ke liye extra protection — code ke saath ek secret verifier bhi hota hai, taaki code beech me chori bhi ho jaye to use na kiya ja sake. Aaj PKCE har jagah use karna chahiye.

Kyun safe: Access token kabhi browser URL me nahi aata — sirf server-to-server exchange hota hai.

2. Implicit Flow — purana, ab band

Kaise: Authorization server seedha browser URL me access token bhej deta tha (#access_token=...). SPA (single-page apps) ke liye banaya gaya tha, jab backend nahi hota tha.

Kyun band: Token URL me aata hai — browser history, logs, referrer header me leak ho sakta hai. Refresh token bhi nahi milta tha. OAuth 2.1 ne is flow ko hata diya hai — ab SPA bhi Authorization Code + PKCE use karte hain.

Galat: Aaj bhi Implicit flow use karna — ye deprecated hai. Authorization Code + PKCE use karo.

3. Client Credentials Flow — machine to machine

Kab: Koi user nahi hai — do servers aapas me baat kar rahe hain. Example: Tumhara backend, payment gateway ki API ko call kar raha hai.

Kaise: App apna client ID + client secret bhej ke seedha access token maangti hai. Koi login, koi consent nahi — kyunki user involved hi nahi hai.

Scope: Token sirf wahi kar sakta hai jo us client ko allow hai. Secret ko vault me rakho — leak hua to koi bhi tumhare naam se API call kar sakta hai.

4. Device Code Flow — TV aur IoT ke liye

Kab: Aise devices jinme type karna mushkil hai — Smart TV, printer, IoT device. Kaise: (1) TV ek device code + user code dikhata hai ('TV pe 123-456 dikh raha hai'). (2) Tum phone/computer se ek URL khol ke code dalte ho aur approve karte ho. (3) TV baar-baar server se poochta hai 'approve hua?' — hote hi use access token mil jata hai.

Example: YouTube TV pe login — TV pe code, phone se approve. Password TV pe type nahi karna padta.

Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC): Ek aur purana flow — app seedha username/password leti thi. Ab deprecated hai — kabhi mat use karo, ye OAuth ka point hi khatam kar deta hai.

3. Flows ka comparison

FlowUser involved?Best forStatus
Authorization Code (+PKCE)HaanWeb apps, mobile, SPA✅ Standard
ImplicitHaanPurani SPAs❌ Deprecated (OAuth 2.1)
Client CredentialsNahiServer-to-server✅ Standard
Device CodeHaan (doosre device se)TV, IoT✅ Standard
ROPC (password)HaanLegacy only❌ Deprecated
Authorization Code + PKCE flow (aaj ka standard):
1. App → Google: "login karo" (code_challenge ke saath)
2. User → Google: login + consent
3. Google → App: authorization code (URL me)
4. App → Google: code + code_verifier + client_secret
5. Google → App: access_token + refresh_token
6. App → API: Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

4. Try karo — sahi OAuth flow chuno

4 alag apps hain. Har ek ke liye sahi OAuth flow chuno — galat flow chunoge to security hole ban jayega.

  1. 1. Web app — 'Login with Google'
  2. 2. Mobile app — Google Drive access
  3. 3. Backend server — payment API call
  4. 4. Smart TV — YouTube login
  5. 5. Galat flow — Implicit try kiya

5. OAuth roles — kaun kaun hota hai?

RoleKaunExample
Resource OwnerUser — jiska data haiTum
ClientApp — jo access maang rahi haiPhotoPrint app
Authorization ServerJo permission deta haiGoogle accounts
Resource ServerJahan data hai (API)Google Drive API

Scope: Permission ki limit — drive.readonly matlab sirf padh sakte ho, drive matlab badal bhi sakte ho. Hamesha minimum scope maango.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Implicit flow use karna: Deprecated hai — token URL me leak hota hai. Authorization Code + PKCE use karo.
  2. PKCE ke bina mobile app: Public clients me client secret nahi hota — PKCE hi ekmatra protection hai. Bina PKCE ke code chori ho sakta hai.
  3. Client secret ko frontend me rakhna: Secret sirf backend/vault me — JS code me likha secret public hai.
  4. Zaroorat se zyada scope maangna: 'Sirf photos padhni hain' to drive.readonly maango, poora drive nahi. User bharosa kho dega.
  5. OAuth ko login samajhna: OAuth authorization hai. User ki pehchan ke liye OIDC (ID token) use karo.

7. Interview corner

Q: OAuth 2.0 ke main flows kaunse hain?

Authorization Code (+PKCE) — web/mobile apps ke liye standard; Client Credentials — server-to-server; Device Code — TV/IoT; Implicit — deprecated hai. Har flow ek alag situation ke liye hai.

Q: PKCE kya hai aur kyun zaroori hai?

PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) Authorization Code flow ki extra protection hai — public clients (mobile/SPA) ke liye, jinke paas client secret nahi hota. Code ke saath ek verifier hota hai — code chori bhi ho jaye to verifier ke bina token nahi milta.

Q: Implicit flow deprecated kyun hai?

Kyunki access token seedha browser URL me aata tha — history, logs aur referrer header me leak ho sakta tha, aur refresh token bhi nahi milta tha. Ab SPA bhi Authorization Code + PKCE use karte hain.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Web app ke liye sabse safe OAuth flow kaunsa hai?

  • Implicit flow
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Authorization Code + PKCE
  • ROPC (password flow)
  • Koi flow nahi

Sawaal 2: Client Credentials flow kab use hota hai?

  • Jab user login karta hai
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Jab do servers aapas me baat karte hain, bina user ke
  • Jab TV pe login karna hai
  • Jab password bhool gaye
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: OAuth = authorization (kya kar sakte ho); standard flow Authorization Code + PKCE hai; Implicit aur ROPC deprecated hain; Client Credentials server-to-server ke liye, Device Code TV/IoT ke liye.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/oauth-20-flows.md
← PichhlaWhat is a Cookie?Agla →Top Network Security Cheatsheet
14Security (Part 2)

Top Network Security Cheatsheet

Network security ka poora syllabus ek page me — cheatsheet style: har attack, uska bachao, aur wo tool ya technique jo use rokti hai. Interview se pehle revise karne ke liye ya apne system ko check karne ke liye — ye page ek ready reckoner hai.

1. Network security — sheher ka suraksha manual

Ek sheher ki suraksha ka manual ek page me likha ho: border pe kya check hoga, andar police kahan hogi, emergency me kya karna hai, har mohalle ka alag rule. Network security cheatsheet wahi manual hai — har layer, har attack, har defense, ek jagah.

Is page ko revision ki tarah use karo: har section ko padho, aur apne system se poochho — 'ye humne lagaya hai ya nahi?' Jo nahi lagaya, wo tumhara agla kaam hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Layer 1 — Network (Firewall, Segmentation)

Firewall: Traffic filter — default deny, sirf zaroori ports kholo. Segmentation: Network ko hisson me baanto — web, app, DB alag segments, beech me firewall rules. DMZ: Public servers alag zone me.

IDS/IPS: Attack ko pehchan ke alert/block karo. DDoS protection: CDN + rate limiting + cloud scrubbing.

Check: Kya tumhare saare ports scan karke dekhe gaye hain? Kya internal network segmented hai ya ek hi bada hall hai?

Layer 2 — Identity (Auth, MFA, Zero Trust)

MFA: Har important account pe — TOTP app ya hardware key, SMS nahi. SSO: Ek login, kai apps — IdP pe strong MFA. Least privilege: Har user/service ko sirf utna access jitna zaroori hai.

Zero Trust: 'Andar ka network safe hai' — ye maan na band karo. Har request verify karo — user, device, location, sab.

Secrets: API keys vault me, rotation ke saath, code me kabhi nahi.

Layer 3 — Data (Encryption, DLP)

In transit: TLS 1.2+ har jagah, HSTS on. At rest: Disk/DB encryption (AES-256), sensitive fields alag se encrypt/tokenize.

DLP (Data Loss Prevention): Sensitive data bahar na jaye — email/USB/cloud upload pe rules. Backups: Encrypted, tested restore, offline copy.

Masking: Logs aur UI me sirf aakhri 4 digit dikhao.

Layer 4 — App + Monitoring (WAF, SIEM)

WAF: Web Application Firewall — SQLi, XSS jaise HTTP attacks rokta hai. Secure coding: Input validation, parameterized queries, output encoding, CSP.

SIEM: Saare logs ek jagah — anomaly detection, alerts. Patching: Updates turant lagao — purane version me jaani kamzoriyan hoti hain.

Incident response: Plan pehle se likha ho — detect, contain, eradicate, recover, learn.

3. Attack → Defense cheatsheet

AttackKaise hota haiDefense
PhishingFake email/link se credential churanaMFA, email filtering, awareness training
Malware / RansomwareMalicious file/link se system infectAntivirus/EDR, backups (offline), patching
DDoSTraffic flood se server giranaCDN, rate limiting, WAF, cloud scrubbing
SQL InjectionInput me SQL codeParameterized queries, WAF
XSSScript doosre user ke browser meOutput encoding, CSP, HttpOnly cookies
CSRFDoosri site se authenticated requestSameSite cookies, CSRF tokens
MITMBeech me traffic sunna/badalnaHTTPS, HSTS, certificate pinning, VPN
Brute forceBaar-baar password guessRate limiting, lockout, CAPTCHA, MFA
Insider threatAndar ka aadmi data churayeLeast privilege, audit logs, offboarding
Zero-dayUnknown vulnerabilityDefense in depth, IPS, fast patching

4. Try karo — security audit karo

Ek startup ka network audit karo. 5 checks hain — har ek me dekho kya galat hai aur sahi fix kya hai.

  1. 1. Ports scan karo
  2. 2. Password policy check karo
  3. 3. Logs dekho
  4. 4. Backup test karo
  5. 5. Ex-employee access check karo

5. Tools cheatsheet — kaunsa tool kya karta hai?

KaamTools (examples)
FirewallpfSense, AWS Security Groups, iptables
WAFCloudflare, AWS WAF, ModSecurity
IDS/IPSSnort, Suricata, Zeek
SIEMSplunk, Elastic SIEM, Wazuh
Vulnerability scanNessus, OpenVAS, Trivy
SecretsHashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager
EndpointCrowdStrike, SentinelOne, OSSEC

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Cheatsheet ko padh ke bhool jana: Checklist ka fayda tabhi hai jab use action me badlo — har hafte ek item fix karo.
  2. Sirf tools kharidna: SIEM kharid liya, par alerts koi nahi dekhta — tool bina process ke bekaar hai.
  3. Internal network ko safe maan lena: Zero trust rakho — insider aur lateral movement se hi bade breaches hote hain.
  4. Patching ko taalna: 'Kal karenge' — kal tak attacker aaj ka patch exploit kar chuka hota hai.
  5. Incident plan ka na hona: Breach ke waqt plan banana bahut der hai. Plan likho, drill karo.

7. Interview corner

Q: Network security ke main layers kaunse hain?

Network (firewall, segmentation, DMZ), Identity (MFA, SSO, least privilege), Data (encryption, DLP, backups), aur Application + Monitoring (WAF, secure coding, SIEM). Har layer pe alag defense — defense in depth.

Q: Cheatsheet me sabse important cheez kya hai?

Default deny aur least privilege — sirf jo chahiye, wahi allow karo. Aur monitoring — attack hoga, sawaal sirf 'kab pata chalega' hai. Bina detection ke baaki sab adhoora hai.

Q: Ek chhoti company ko pehle 3 security kaam kaunse karne chahiye?

(1) MFA har jagah mandatory karo. (2) Saare software update karo aur backup ka restore test karo. (3) Firewall default deny + sirf zaroori ports kholo. Ye teen kaam 80% attacks rok dete hain.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Database ka port (3306) internet pe khula hona kyun galat hai?

  • Ye slow hota hai
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Koi bhi internet se DB se connect karne ki koshish kar sakta hai
  • Ye mehenga hai
  • Ye backup rokta hai

Sawaal 2: SIEM ka main kaam kya hai?

  • Password banana
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Saare logs ek jagah laake attack detect karna aur alert dena
  • Website banana
  • Email bhejna
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Network security = 4 layers (network, identity, data, app+monitoring) + defense in depth; default deny, least privilege, MFA, patching aur tested backups — yehi 80% security hai.

7 OSI layers — har layer ke attacks (original guide se)

Guide ka diagram 7 OSI model layers me possible network attacks dikhata hai:

LayerAttacks
Application LayerPushing, Malware injection, DDoS attacks
Presentation LayerEncoding/decoding vulnerabilities, Format string attacks, Malicious code injection
Session LayerSession hijacking, Session fixation attacks, Brute force attacks
Transport LayerMan-in-the-middle attacks, SYN/ACK flood
Network LayerIP spoofing, Route table manipulation, DDoS attacks
Data Link LayerMAC address spoofing, ARP spoofing, VLAN hopping
Physical LayerWiretapping, Physical tampering, Electromagnetic interference

Har layer ke apne attacks hain — isliye defense bhi har layer pe chahiye: ek hi firewall ya ek hi tool kaafi nahi hota.

Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/top-network-security-cheatsheet.md
← PichhlaOAuth 2.0 FlowsAgla →What is SSO (Single Sign-On)?
15Security (Part 2)

What is SSO (Single Sign-On)?

Roz 10 apps kholte ho — Gmail, Slack, Jira, GitHub — aur har ek me alag password? SSO (Single Sign-On) ka matlab hai: ek baar login karo, saari apps khul jaayein. Peeche ek Identity Provider hota hai jo tumhari pehchan ki guarantee deta hai. Is page me SSO ka poora flow samjho.

1. SSO — campus pass wali kahani

Socho ek bada campus hai — library, canteen, gym, lab — har jagah alag gate hai. Bina SSO ke har gate pe tumhe apna ID card + password dikhana padta. SSO ke saath tum ek baar main gate pe login karte ho, aur tumhe ek campus pass milta hai. Har building ka guard pass dekh ke andar jaane deta hai — dobara password nahi mangta.

Yahan Identity Provider (IdP) main gate hai — Google, Okta, Azure AD. Apps (Service Providers) ko IdP pe bharosa hai: 'Agar IdP kehta hai ye Priya hai, to hum maante hain.'

Ek line me: SSO = ek IdP pe login, saari connected apps me entry. Password ek jagah, MFA ek jagah, logout ek jagah.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

SSO kaise kaam karta hai? — step by step

1) Tum Slack kholte ho (pehli baar). 2) Slack kehta hai 'tum login nahi ho — IdP (Google) pe jao'. 3) Tum Google pe login karte ho (password + 2FA). 4) Google ek token/assertion (SAML ya OIDC) banata hai — 'Ye Priya hai, ye uska email hai'. 5) Tum wapas Slack pe aate ho, token leke. 6) Slack token verify karta hai → tum andar ho.

7) Ab tum Jira kholte ho — Jira bhi tumhe Google pe bhejta hai, par Google kehta hai 'ye pehle se login hai' — bina password ke naya token mil jata hai → Jira bhi khul gaya. Yahi SSO hai.

SAML vs OIDC — do protocols

SAML (older, enterprise): XML-based, enterprise apps (Salesforce, Workday) me common. IdP ek signed XML assertion bhejta hai. Browser-based flow hai.

OIDC (newer, modern): OAuth 2.0 ke upar bana hai, JSON/JWT use karta hai. Web + mobile dono me chalta hai. 'Login with Google' OIDC hi hai — ID token (JWT) me user ki pehchan hoti hai.

Kaunsa chunein: Naya system bana rahe ho to OIDC. Enterprise legacy apps ke saath SAML. Kai IdPs dono support karte hain.

SSO ke fayde

Users ke liye: Ek password yaad rakho, har app me dobara login nahi. Security ke liye: Password ek jagah strong + MFA ek jagah — har app ka alag kamzor password nahi. IT ke liye: Employee nikla to ek jagah se access band — saari apps se logout. Onboarding bhi aasan — ek account banao, saari apps mil jaayein.

Compliance: Har login ka central log banta hai — audit aasan ho jata hai. Kisne, kab, kis app me login kiya — sab ek jagah.

SSO ke khatre — single point of failure

IdP hack hua to? Ek IdP compromise hua to attacker saari apps me ghus sakta hai. Isliye IdP pe sabse strong security chahiye — hardware-key MFA, anomaly detection, backup login method.

IdP down hua to? Saari apps band — koi login nahi kar sakta. Isliye IdP ki high availability aur backup IdP ka plan zaroori hai.

Session hijack: SSO session chori hua to saari apps khul jaati hain — short session expiry aur device verification zaroori hai.

Galat: SSO laga ke MFA bhool jana — SSO + bina MFA ke matlab ek password se saari apps ka darwaza khula hai.

3. SSO flow — ek diagram ki tarah

User → Slack: "Slack kholo"
Slack → User: "Login nahi ho — Google (IdP) pe jao"
User → Google: login (password + 2FA) ✓
Google → User: token (SAML assertion / OIDC ID token)
User → Slack: token leke wapas
Slack: token verify kiya → "Welcome, Priya!" ✓
User → Jira: "Jira kholo"
Jira → User: "Google pe jao"
Google: "Ye pehle se login hai!" → naya token, bina password ke
User → Jira: token leke wapas → Jira khul gaya ✓
# Ek login, do apps — yahi SSO hai

Logout: Ek jagah se logout karo to IdP saari apps ko batata hai (Single Logout) — saari sessions band. Par har app ise support nahi karti — check karo.

4. Try karo — ek login se 3 apps kholo

Tum ek naye employee ho. Google (IdP) se login karo aur dekho SSO kaise kaam karta hai — phir logout karo aur dekho kya hota hai.

  1. 1. Slack kholo — pehli app
  2. 2. Jira kholo — dobara login?
  3. 3. GitHub kholo
  4. 4. Logout karo — ek jagah se
  5. 5. Attacker IdP password churata hai

5. SSO vs OAuth vs SAML vs OIDC

CheezKya haiKaam
SSOConceptEk login, kai apps
SAMLProtocol (XML)Enterprise SSO
OIDCProtocol (JWT, OAuth pe)Modern SSO + login
OAuthProtocolAuthorization (data access), login nahi

Yaad rakhna: SSO ek idea hai; SAML aur OIDC use implement karne ke protocols hain; OAuth authorization ke liye hai, SSO ke liye OIDC use hota hai.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. SSO laga ke MFA bhoolna: Ek password se saari apps — MFA ke bina SSO khatarnak hai.
  2. IdP ko single point of failure bhoolna: IdP down ya hack hua to sab band. Backup aur strong security rakho.
  3. Single Logout ko assume kar lena: Har app SLO support nahi karti — logout ke baad bhi kuch sessions chalti reh sakti hain. Check karo.
  4. Har app ko SSO me daal dena bina soche: Sensitive apps (finance, prod access) pe extra step (step-up auth) rakho — SSO login kaafi nahi.
  5. Ex-employee ka IdP account on chhodna: Offboarding pe IdP account band karte hi saari apps se access band hona chahiye — ye SSO ka sabse bada fayda hai, use karo.

7. Interview corner

Q: SSO kya hai aur kaise kaam karta hai?

Single Sign-On matlab ek baar login karo, saari connected apps bina dobara login ke khul jaayein. Peeche ek Identity Provider (IdP) hota hai — app tumhe IdP pe bhejti hai, IdP login ke baad ek token (SAML/OIDC) deta hai, app use verify karke andar jaane deti hai.

Q: SAML aur OIDC me farq?

SAML XML-based purana enterprise protocol hai; OIDC OAuth 2.0 ke upar bana JSON/JWT-based modern protocol hai, jo web aur mobile dono me chalta hai. Naye systems me OIDC prefer karte hain.

Q: SSO ka sabse bada khatra kya hai?

Single point of failure — IdP compromise ya down hone par saari apps affect hoti hain. Isliye IdP pe strong MFA, monitoring aur high availability zaroori hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: SSO ka main fayda kya hai?

  • Har app ka alag password yaad rakhna
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Ek baar login karo, saari connected apps khul jaayein
  • Internet fast ho jata hai
  • Password ki zaroorat hi nahi

Sawaal 2: SSO me user ki pehchan ki guarantee kaun deta hai?

  • Har app khud
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Identity Provider (IdP)
  • Browser
  • Wi-Fi router
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: SSO = ek IdP pe login, saari apps me entry (SAML/OIDC protocols); fayda: ek password, ek jagah MFA, ek jagah se offboarding; khatra: IdP hi single point of failure hai — isliye uspe sabse strong security rakho.

SSO ka 14-step flow — How SSO Works (original guide se)

Ek dost ko baar-baar alag-alag websites se sign out hone ki pareshani hui — har baar bhoole hue passwords yaad karne padte the. SSO ye pareshani khatm karta hai. Basically, Single Sign-On (SSO) ek authentication scheme hai — user ek hi ID se alag-alag systems me login kar sakta hai. Neeche wala diagram dikhata hai ki SSO kaise kaam karta hai:

  1. Step 1: User Gmail (ya koi email service) kholta hai. Gmail dekhta hai user logged in nahi hai, to use SSO authentication server pe redirect karta hai. Server bhi dekhta hai user logged in nahi hai, to user SSO login page pe redirect hota hai, jahan wo apne login credentials dalta hai.
  2. Steps 2-3: SSO authentication server credentials validate karta hai, user ke liye global session banata hai, aur ek token banata hai.
  3. Steps 4-7: Gmail token ko SSO authentication server pe validate karta hai. Authentication server Gmail system ko register karta hai aur "valid" return karta hai. Gmail protected resource user ko de deta hai.
  4. Step 8: Gmail se user doosri Google-owned website pe jata hai — example ke liye YouTube.
  5. Steps 9-10: YouTube dekhta hai user logged in nahi hai, to authentication maangta hai. SSO authentication server dekhta hai user pehle se logged in hai, to token return kar deta hai.
  6. Steps 11-14: YouTube token ko SSO authentication server pe validate karta hai. Authentication server YouTube system ko register karta hai aur "valid" return karta hai. YouTube protected resource user ko de deta hai.

Process complete ho gaya — user ko dobara login nahi karna pada aur use apna account wapas mil gaya.

Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/v1what-is-sso-single-sign-on.md
← PichhlaTop Network Security CheatsheetAgla →Session, Cookie, JWT, Token, SSO, and OAuth 2.0 Explained
16Security (Part 2)

Session, Cookie, JWT, Token, SSO, and OAuth 2.0 Explained

Auth ke 6 shabd — Session, Cookie, JWT, Token, SSO, OAuth 2.0 — har interview me aate hain, aur har baar confuse karte hain. Ye page in chheh ko ek hi badi kahani me jodta hai, taaki tum inke beech ka farq aur rishta dono samajh sako.

1. Chheh concepts, ek kahani — ek sheher ki kahani

Socho ek sheher hai jisme kai buildings hain. Session = har building ke gate pe register — guard tumhara naam likh ke yaad rakhta hai. Cookie = tumhare haath ka stamp — gate pe dikhao, andar jao. Token/JWT = tumhara ID card — naam, photo, expiry aur mohar sab likhi hai; guard card dekh ke jaane deta hai, register nahi dekhta. SSO = ek hi campus pass se saari buildings me entry. OAuth = tum kisi dost ko kehte ho 'meri building se mera ek file le aao' — use tumhari chaabi nahi, ek limited slip dete ho.

Yaad rakhne ka tareeka: Session/Token/JWT = tum kaun ho (authentication, login state). Cookie = us pehchan ko le jaane ka tareeka. SSO = ek login, kai apps. OAuth = kisi aur ko limited permission (authorization).

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Session — server yaad rakhta hai

Login ke baad server tumhara record apne paas rakhta hai (Redis/DB), aur tumhe ek session ID deta hai — aam taur pe cookie me. Har request pe server ID se lookup karta hai.

Plus: Revoke turant, data server pe safe. Minus: Har request pe lookup, scale ke liye shared store chahiye.

Traditional web apps ka standard hai — simple aur control tumhare haath me.

Cookie — carrier hai, pehchan nahi

Cookie ek storage/transport mechanism hai — server Set-Cookie se data deta hai, browser har request me wapas bhejta hai. Cookie me session ID bhi rakh sakte ho, JWT bhi.

Yaad rakhna: 'Cookie vs Session' galat comparison hai — cookie session ID ko le jaane ka tareeka hai. Sahi comparison 'Session vs JWT' hai.

Cookie pe HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite flags lagao — warna XSS aur CSRF se chori hogi.

JWT aur Token — khud ka saboot

Token ek general shabd hai — access ka saboot. JWT uska ek format hai: Header.Payload.Signature — self-contained, signed, stateless.

Server ko lookup nahi karna padta — signature verify karo, payload padho. Isliye APIs aur microservices me popular hai. Trade-off: Revoke mushkil — short expiry + refresh token use karo. Payload me sensitive data mat rakho (koi bhi decode kar sakta hai).

SSO aur OAuth — upar ki parat

SSO: Ek IdP pe login karo, saari apps khul jaayein (SAML/OIDC protocols). OAuth 2.0: Third-party app ko tumhare data tak limited, scoped access do — bina password diye.

Dono aksar saath aate hain: 'Login with Google' me OAuth + OIDC dono chalte hain — OIDC tumhari pehchan deta hai, OAuth API access deta hai.

Farq: SSO authentication hai (tum kaun ho, kai apps me). OAuth authorization hai (app kya kar sakti hai).

3. Sab kuch ek saath — poora login flow

1. User "Login with Google" dabata hai (OAuth + OIDC)
2. Google (IdP) pe login: password + 2FA
3. Google app ko deta hai: ID token (JWT — tum kaun ho)
   + access token (API access — kya kar sakte ho)
4. App ID token verify karti hai → SESSION banati hai
   (server pe record + cookie me session ID)
5. Ab user app me session cookie se ghumta hai
6. Doosri app kholo → SSO: IdP pe pehle se login ho → bina password ke token
7. Third-party app ko Drive access do → OAuth: scoped access token,
   password kabhi nahi milta, permission kabhi bhi wapas le sakte ho

Ek line me poora stack: OAuth/OIDC = login karwaya, Session/Cookie = login yaad rakha, JWT = APIs ke liye token, SSO = dobara login nahi karna pada.

4. Try karo — ek din, chheh concepts

Ek user ka din dekho: Google se login, do apps, ek third-party app ko permission — har step me kaunsa concept kaam kar raha hai?

  1. 1. 'Login with Google' dabao
  2. 2. App me ghumo — session kaam kar raha hai
  3. 3. Mobile app kholo — JWT kaam kar raha hai
  4. 4. Doosri app kholo — SSO kaam kar raha hai
  5. 5. Third-party app ko Drive access do — OAuth

5. Chheh concepts — ek table me

ConceptKya haiKahan rehta haiKaam
SessionServer-side login recordServer (Redis/DB)Login state yaad rakhna
CookieBrowser storage mechanismBrowserSession ID / token le jaana
JWTSigned token formatClient peStateless authentication
TokenAccess ka saboot (general)Client peAPI access
SSOEk login, kai appsIdP peMultiple apps me login
OAuth 2.0Authorization frameworkTokens, scopedThird-party ko limited access

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Cookie ko authentication samajhna: Cookie sirf carrier hai — asli auth server pe session lookup ya token verify se hoti hai.
  2. OAuth ko login samajhna: OAuth authorization hai. Login ke liye OIDC chahiye.
  3. JWT payload me sensitive data: Payload Base64 hai — koi bhi padh sakta hai. Sirf id, role, expiry rakho.
  4. Session aur JWT ko mix karna: Session revoke turant hota hai, JWT nahi — use case dekh ke chuno.
  5. SSO ke saath MFA bhoolna: Ek password se saari apps — MFA ke bina SSO khatarnak hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: Session, Cookie, JWT, SSO, OAuth — ek line me farq?

Session server-side login record hai; Cookie use le jaane ka tareeka hai; JWT stateless signed token hai; SSO ek login se kai apps hai; OAuth third-party ko limited access dene ka framework hai.

Q: OAuth aur SSO me farq?

SSO authentication hai — ek login se kai apps me entry. OAuth authorization hai — ek app ko user ke data tak limited access. SSO ke peeche aksar OAuth/OIDC hi chalta hai, par purpose alag hai.

Q: Web app ke liye session, mobile app ke liye JWT — kyun?

Web app me browser cookie handle karta hai aur server ko revoke control chahiye — session best hai. Mobile app me cookie nahi hoti aur APIs stateless scale chahiye — JWT natural hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Cookie ka asli kaam kya hai?

  • User ko authenticate karna
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Session ID ya token ko browser se server tak le jaana
  • Password store karna
  • Website banana

Sawaal 2: OAuth 2.0 ka main kaam kya hai?

  • User ko login karwana
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Third-party app ko limited, scoped access dena — bina password ke
  • Password reset karna
  • Website ko fast banana
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Session = server yaad rakhta hai; Cookie = carrier; JWT = stateless signed token; SSO = ek login, kai apps; OAuth = limited permission, password nahi; Authentication (kaun ho) aur Authorization (kya kar sakte ho) alag hain.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/session-cookie-jwt-token-sso-and-oauth-2.md

17Security (Part 2)

OAuth 2.0 Explained With Simple Terms

'Login with Google' — ye button har jagah hai, par peeche kya hota hai? OAuth 2.0 ko simple terms me samjho: tum apna password diye bina, kisi app ko apne data tak limited access kaise dete ho — aur use wapas kaise lete ho.

1. OAuth — valet key wali kahani

Socho tum apni gaadi ek hotel ke valet ko dete ho. Tum use apni asli chaabi nahi dete — tum use ek valet key dete ho, jisse gaadi sirf park ki ja sakti hai, dickey (trunk) nahi khul sakta, aur wo sirf aaj ke liye kaam karti hai.

OAuth wahi valet key hai: tum app ko apna password nahi dete — tum use ek access token dete ho, jisse wo sirf wahi kar sakti hai jo tumne allow kiya (jaise photos padhna), sirf utne time ke liye jitna tumne allow kiya. Aur tum chaaho to valet key wapas le sakte ho — bina apni asli chaabi badle.

Ek line me: OAuth = password diye bina, limited permission dena. Password tumhara hai, token app ka hai — aur token ko kabhi bhi wapas le sakte ho.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

OAuth kya hai? — simple me

OAuth 2.0 ek authorization framework hai — matlab ye decide karta hai ki ek app tumhare data ke saath kya-kya kar sakti hai, tumhare password ke bina.

Example: Tum ek photo printing app ko kehte ho 'meri Google Photos se photos leke print karo'. App ko tumhara Google password nahi milta — use ek token milta hai, jisse wo sirf photos padh sakti hai, sirf 1 ghante ke liye.

Important: OAuth login nahi hai — ye permission hai. 'Login with Google' me OAuth ke upar OIDC chalta hai, jo tumhari pehchan bhi deta hai.

4 roles — kaun kaun hota hai?

1) Resource Owner (tum): Jiska data hai — tum. 2) Client (app): Jo access maang rahi hai — PhotoPrint app. 3) Authorization Server: Jo permission deta hai — Google Accounts. 4) Resource Server: Jahan data hai — Google Photos API.

Tum Authorization Server ko kehte ho 'haan, is app ko meri photos padhne do' — wo app ko token deta hai — app token leke Resource Server se photos leti hai.

Flow — step by step (Authorization Code)

1) Tum app me 'Connect Google Photos' dabate ho. 2) App tumhe Google pe bhejti hai. 3) Tum Google pe login karte ho (agar nahi ho) aur dekhte ho: 'PhotoPrint tumhari photos padhna chahti hai — Allow?' 4) Tum Allow dabate ho. 5) Google app ko ek code deta hai. 6) App code ko token se badal leti hai (server pe). 7) App token se Photos API call karti hai — photos mil gayi!

Scope: Permission ki limit — photos.readonly matlab sirf padh sakti hai, delete nahi. Hamesha minimum scope do.

Token — access aur refresh

Access token: Chhota (1 ghanta), har API call me jata hai (Authorization: Bearer ...). Expire ho jaye to dobara maangna padta hai.

Refresh token: Lamba (din/mahine), sirf naya access token lene ke liye use hota hai. Server pe securely store hota hai.

Revoke: Tum Google settings → Third-party access me jaake permission wapas le sakte ho — turant token bekaar ho jata hai. Password badalne ki zaroorat nahi — kyunki password app ko mila hi nahi tha!

Sahi: App ko sirf utni permission do jitni chahiye, aur waqt-waqt pe third-party access check karo.

3. OAuth vs Password sharing — farq

CheezPassword share karnaOAuth token
App ko kya milta hai?Tumhara password — sab kuchLimited token — sirf allow kiya kaam
Permission wapas lenaPassword badalna padegaEk click me revoke
ExpiryKabhi nahi1 ghanta (access), revoke possible
ScopeSab kuchSirf jo allow kiya

Yaad rakhna: Koi app tumse password maange to wo OAuth use nahi kar rahi — wo galat kar rahi hai. Sahi app hamesha tumhe Google/Facebook pe bhejegi, password khud nahi maangegi.

4. Try karo — ek app ko permission do

Ek photo printing app tumhari Google Photos access karna chahti hai. Poora OAuth flow dekho — aur phir permission wapas bhi lo.

  1. 1. App permission maangti hai
  2. 2. Tum Allow dabate ho
  3. 3. App zyada maangti hai
  4. 4. Permission wapas lo
  5. 5. Password share kiya hota to?

5. OAuth ke main flows — ek table me

FlowKab
Authorization Code (+PKCE)Web/mobile apps — standard
Client CredentialsServer-to-server, koi user nahi
Device CodeTV/IoT — type karna mushkil
Implicit / ROPCDeprecated — mat use karo

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. OAuth ko login samajhna: OAuth authorization hai. Login (pehchan) ke liye OIDC chahiye.
  2. App ko password dena: Sahi app kabhi password nahi maangti — wo tumhe Google pe bhejegi. Password maange to bhaag jao.
  3. Zaroorat se zyada scope dena: 'Photos padhni hain' to sirf photos ki permission do, poora account nahi.
  4. Third-party access ko kabhi check na karna: Saal bhar purani apps ko access diya hua hai — waqt-waqt pe Google settings check karo aur bekaar access hatao.
  5. Token ko URL me leak karna: Access token ko kabhi URL ya logs me mat bhejo — Authorization header me bhejo.

7. Interview corner

Q: OAuth 2.0 kya hai, simple terms me?

OAuth 2.0 ek authorization framework hai — tum kisi app ko apne data tak limited access dete ho, bina password diye. App ko ek access token milta hai (scope + expiry ke saath), aur tum use kabhi bhi revoke kar sakte ho. Password app ko kabhi nahi milta.

Q: OAuth aur password sharing me farq?

Password share karne se app ko sab kuch mil jata hai aur wapas lene ke liye password badalna padta hai. OAuth me app ko sirf allow kiya kaam karne wala token milta hai, expiry hoti hai, aur ek click me revoke ho jata hai.

Q: 'Login with Google' me OAuth ka kya role hai?

'Login with Google' me OAuth authorization deta hai aur uske upar OIDC authentication deta hai — ID token (JWT) se app ko tumhari pehchan milti hai. Sirf OAuth se login nahi hota, OIDC chahiye.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: OAuth me app ko kya milta hai?

  • Tumhara password
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Limited scope aur expiry wala access token
  • Tumhara poora account
  • Tumhari fingerprint

Sawaal 2: OAuth permission wapas lene ke liye kya karna padta hai?

  • Password badalna
  • ✅ Sahi jawab: Settings se app ka access revoke karna — ek click
  • App delete karna
  • Kuch nahi ho sakta
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: OAuth = password diye bina limited permission (valet key); 4 roles: tum, app, authorization server, resource server; scope minimum rakho; permission ek click me wapas lo; login ke liye OIDC chahiye.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/oauth-2-explained-with-siple-terms.md

Interactive Labs

4 labs — mushkil concepts ko haath se aazmao. Har lab ka output yahin live dikhta hai.

LABJWT Inspector — token kholo, expiry check karo

Neeche sample JWT daala hai (ya apna token paste karo). Decode dabate hi header aur payload dikhenge, aur pata chalega token expire hua ya valid hai. Signature ko yahan verify nahi kar sakte — uske liye secret chahiye hota hai, jo client ke paas kabhi nahi hona chahiye.


LABOAuth 2.0 Flow Stepper — kaunsa flow, kis step me kya hota hai

Flow chuno, phir "Agla step" dabate jao — har step me dikhega kaun kisse kya bhejta hai. Authorization Code + PKCE aaj ka standard hai; Implicit flow purana hai aur avoid karna chahiye.


LABPassword Storage Lab — plain vs hash vs salted hash

Password likho aur dekho: plain text me store karna, sirf SHA-256 hash karna, aur salt ke saath hash karna — teeno me kya farak padta hai. Hash yahan browser me hi real SHA-256 se banta hai. Salt ek random value hai jo har user ke liye alag hoti hai.


LABSite Safe Hai Ya Nahi — URL checker

URL likho aur check karo — kya site pe login karna safe hai? Lab HTTPS, domain spelling, aur certificate warning teenon check karta hai. Neeche diye examples pe bhi try karo: goggle.com, http wali site, ya apni bank ki site.

19End Matter

Interview FAQs

12 FAQs — aaj ke era ke system design interviews me poochhe jaane wale sawaal, seedhe jawab ke saath. Sawaal par tap karo, jawab khulega.

01JWT aur session-based authentication me kya farak hai, aur kab kya use karna chahiye?
Session-based auth me server session store karta hai aur browser ko sirf ek session ID (cookie) deta hai — har request pe server session dhoondhta hai, isliye revoke karna aasan hai par server stateful hota hai. JWT stateless hai — token me hi saari info hoti hai, server kuch store nahi karta, isliye scale karna aasan hai. Par JWT ko revoke karna mushkil hai (expiry tak valid rehta hai), isliye short expiry + refresh token use karte hain. Rule: monolith ya single-server app ho to session kaafi hai; microservices ya mobile API ho to JWT behtar hai.
02OAuth 2.0 ke flows kaunse hain, aur Authorization Code + PKCE kyun best mana jata hai?
OAuth 2.0 ke main flows hain: Authorization Code, Authorization Code + PKCE, Client Credentials, aur Implicit (purana). Authorization Code + PKCE aaj ka standard hai kyunki code_challenge/code_verifier se authorization code chori hone par bhi attacker token nahi le sakta — verifier ke bina code bekaar hai. Client Credentials sirf machine-to-machine ke liye hai (koi user nahi). Implicit flow me token seedha URL fragment me aata hai, isliye leak hona aasan hai — OAuth 2.1 ne use hata diya hai. Interview me PKCE ka full form (Proof Key for Code Exchange) aur uska kaam batana important hai.
03Passkey password se behtar kaise hai, aur WebAuthn ka isme kya role hai?
Passkey public-key cryptography pe chalti hai: tumhare device pe ek private key banti hai (jo kabhi device se bahar nahi jati) aur server pe sirf public key store hoti hai. Login ke time server ek challenge bhejta hai, device use private key se sign karta hai (fingerprint/face se unlock karke). Phishing fail hoti hai kyunki fake site ka domain sign nahi hoga, aur server hack hone par bhi password leak nahi hota (public key bekaar hai). WebAuthn wahi standard hai jo browser aur device ke beech ye kaam karwata hai. Password ka sabse bada dushman — reuse aur phishing — dono passkey me khatm ho jate hain.
04HTTPS hone ke baad bhi phishing kaise hoti hai?
HTTPS sirf connection ko encrypt karta hai, site ki neeyat ko nahi batata. Koi bhi free certificate (Let's Encrypt se, 2 minute me) le kar goggle.com jaisi fake site bana sakta hai — browser me taala dikhega, par site fake hogi. Certificate sirf ye verify karta hai ki domain kiska hai (DV certificate me to sirf domain ownership check hota hai). Isliye taala dekh ke bharosa mat karo: domain ko akshar-akshar padho, certificate warning aaye to ruk jao, aur login link hamesha official app ya khud type kiye hue URL se kholo, email ke link se nahi.
05Cookie attributes HttpOnly, Secure aur SameSite kya karte hain?
HttpOnly cookie ko JavaScript se padha nahi ja sakta — XSS attack se session token chori nahi hota. Secure ka matlab hai cookie sirf HTTPS connection pe bheji jayegi, HTTP pe nahi — network pe leak nahi hogi. SameSite control karta hai ki cookie cross-site request ke saath jaye ya nahi: Strict (sirf same-site), Lax (top-level navigation pe allow), None (cross-site allow, par Secure ke saath hi). Teeno ko ek saath use karna best practice hai: HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax. Ye session hijacking aur CSRF dono ko mushkil banata hai.
06Symmetric aur asymmetric encryption me kya farak hai, aur dono ek saath kaise use hote hain?
Symmetric encryption me ek hi key se encrypt aur decrypt hota hai (AES) — fast hai, par key ko dono taraf safely pahunchana mushkil hai. Asymmetric me do keys hoti hain: public key (sabko pata) aur private key (sirf tumhare paas) — RSA/ECC slow hain par key exchange safe hai. Real systems dono ko milate hain: TLS handshake me asymmetric encryption se ek session key exchange hoti hai, phir saara data usi session key se symmetric encryption (AES) me chalta hai — speed bhi, safety bhi. Interview me ye hybrid approach zaroor batana.
07SSO kaise kaam karta hai, aur SAML aur OIDC me kya farak hai?
SSO (Single Sign-On) me ek Identity Provider (IdP) tumhe ek baar authenticate karta hai, phir tum bina dobara login kiye saari connected apps use kar sakte ho. Flow: app tumhe IdP pe bhejti hai, tum login karte ho, IdP ek token/assertion deta hai, app use verify karke tumhe andar le leti hai. SAML purana XML-based standard hai (enterprise apps me common), OIDC modern JSON/JWT-based hai (OAuth 2.0 ke upar bana hai, web/mobile apps me standard). Dono ka goal ek hi hai — ek login, saari apps. Logout aur session expiry ka dhyaan rakhna SSO me sabse tricky hissa hota hai.
08DevSecOps ka matlab kya hai, aur shift-left security kya hoti hai?
DevSecOps ka matlab hai security ko development pipeline ke har step me daalna — aakhir me alag se security check karne ki jagah, shuru se hi. Shift-left ka matlab hai security ko "left" (shuru) ki taraf le jana: code likhte time linter se secret scan, pull request pe dependency vulnerability check, CI me SAST (static analysis) aur container scan, deploy se pehle DAST. Isse bug production me jaane se pehle, saste me pakda jata hai — baad me fix karna 10-100 guna mehenga padta hai. DevSecOps koi tool nahi, ek culture hai: har developer security ka zimmedar hai.
09Firewall ke main types kaunse hain, aur kaunsa kab use hota hai?
Packet-filtering firewall sirf IP/port dekh ke allow/block karta hai — fast par andha hai. Stateful firewall connection ki state yaad rakhta hai — sirf valid response wapas aane deta hai. Application-layer (proxy) firewall HTTP jaise protocol ko samajh ke filter karta hai — slow par gehra. Next-gen firewall (NGFW) me intrusion prevention, app awareness aur threat intelligence bhi hoti hai. Cloud me security groups (AWS) aur WAF (web application firewall) use hote hain — WAF SQL injection aur XSS jaise web attacks rokta hai. Interview me OSI layer ke hisaab se firewall batana achha lagta hai.
10VPN ke types kya hain — remote access, site-to-site, personal aur cloud VPN me kya farak hai?
Remote Access VPN user ko office network se jodta hai (ghar se office tools) — OpenVPN/WireGuard use hota hai, har user authenticate hota hai. Site-to-Site VPN do offices ko permanent tunnel se jodta hai (IPsec) — user ko kuch karna nahi padta. Personal/Commercial VPN (NordVPN jaise) user ko internet se jodta hai privacy ke liye — provider tumhara traffic dekh sakta hai, isliye no-log policy zaroori hai. Cloud VPN user/office ko cloud VPC se jodta hai (AWS Client VPN). Modern alternative ZTNA hai — poora network kholne ki jagah har app ke liye alag verified access.
112FA aur TOTP (Google Authenticator) kaise kaam karta hai?
2FA ka matlab hai login ke liye do cheezein: kuch jo tum jaante ho (password) + kuch jo tumhare paas hai (phone/app). TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) me server aur tumhara app ek secret share karte hain — dono us secret aur current time (30-second window) se ek 6-digit code banate hain. Code match hua to login. Internet ki zaroorat nahi, kyunki time hi sync ka kaam karta hai. SMS-based 2FA se behtar hai kyunki SIM-swap attack se code chori nahi hota. Interview me ye bhi batana: backup codes kyun zaroori hain (phone kho jaye to account lock na ho).
12JWT ko revoke kaise karte hain, agar wo stateless hai to?
Ye JWT ki sabse badi kamzori hai — token expire hone tak valid rehta hai, server use rok nahi sakta. Solutions: (1) Short expiry — access token 5-15 minute ka rakho, refresh token se naya lo. (2) Blocklist — logout pe token ka jti (JWT ID) ek blocklist (Redis) me daalo aur har request pe check karo — thoda state wapas aa jata hai, par sirf revoked tokens ke liye. (3) Refresh token rotation — har refresh pe purana token invalid karo, reuse dikhe to saare tokens revoke karo. (4) Version/epoch claim — user ke record me ek version number rakho, password change pe version badha do, purane tokens invalid. Interview me ye trade-off batana: pure stateless vs practical security.
